chunks.title: 1. What a room is
chunks.label: One room, many agents: herdr-room in / out · 1. What a room is
chunks.text:
## 1. What a room is

herdr nests from the outside in: session > space (the CLI says workspace) > tab > pane > agent.

A **room** is one space whose single tab shows several agents at once, for example a team desk on the left and its members on the right. `herdr-room` moves the real panes and never starts a new agent, so you can go in and out as often as you like.

```
$ herdr-room --help | head -8
  herdr-room in  <room> [member ...] [--layout fib|cols|rows|main] [--ratio R] [--session S] [--dry]
  herdr-room out <room> [member ...] [--session S] [--dry]   (members given: only they leave)
  herdr-room list
  herdr-room rename <room> <new-name> [--session S]   (space label, tab label and saved state)
```

chunks.title: 2. Set up a team: one space for main, one per worktree
chunks.label: One room, many agents: herdr-room in / out · 2. Set up a team: one space for main, one per worktree
chunks.text:
## 2. Set up a team: one space for main, one per worktree

Make main's space with `workspace create`, but open each worktree with `worktree open`: herdr nests a space under its repo in the sidebar only when the space is bound to a worktree.

```bash
herdr --session roomlab workspace create --cwd /tmp/roomlab/team --label desk --no-focus
herdr --session roomlab worktree open --cwd /tmp/roomlab/team \
  --path /tmp/roomlab/team/wt/member-a --label member-a --no-focus
```

```
{"space":"w2","pane":"w2:p1"}
{"space":"w3","label":"member-a","linked":true}
{"space":"w4","label":"member-b","linked":true}
```

Name every agent and address members by name, never by pane id: pane ids change on every move.

```
w2:p1  desk      idle  team
w3:p1  member-a  idle  team/wt/member-a
w4:p1  member-b  idle  team/wt/member-b
```

chunks.title: 3. Room in: always `--dry` first
chunks.label: One room, many agents: herdr-room in / out · 3. Room in: always `--dry` first
chunks.text:
## 3. Room in: always `--dry` first

```bash
herdr-room in team desk member-a member-b --layout fib --session roomlab --dry
```

```
room 'team' · session roomlab · layout fib · 3 members: desk, member-a, member-b
  plan  herdr --session roomlab pane move w2:p1 --new-workspace --label team ...
  plan  herdr --session roomlab pane move w3:p1 --new-tab --workspace <room> --label scratch ...
  ...
  --dry: nothing was moved (5 moves planned)
```

`--dry` moves nothing; it prints the plan. When the plan is right, run it for real:

```bash
herdr-room in team desk member-a member-b --layout fib --session roomlab
```

```
  name  w5:p1 = desk
  name  w5:p2 = member-a
  name  w5:p3 = member-b
  saved ~/.local/state/herdr-room/roomlab__team.json
  rect  w5:p1    x=0    y=0   57x46
  rect  w5:p2    x=57   y=0   56x23
  rect  w5:p3    x=57   y=23  56x23
```

Layout `fib`: the first member takes the left half at full height, each next one half of what is left, turning right then down (3 members: left | top right / bottom right). The others are `cols`, `rows` and `main` (the first member a wide left column of share `--ratio`). Note that the pane ids went from w2/w3/w4 to w5:p1-p3.

chunks.title: 4. The room remembers itself in a state file
chunks.label: One room, many agents: herdr-room in / out · 4. The room remembers itself in a state file
chunks.text:
## 4. The room remembers itself in a state file

```
$ herdr-room list | rg roomlab
roomlab      team             fib   OPEN  desk · member-a · member-b   (saved 2026-10-31T21:02:02+0700)
```

`~/.local/state/herdr-room/<session>__<room>.json` keeps the layout, the members (path, pane, name) and the time, so the same room can be rebuilt.

chunks.title: 5. Room out: everyone back to a space of their own
chunks.label: One room, many agents: herdr-room in / out · 5. Room out: everyone back to a space of their own
chunks.text:
## 5. Room out: everyone back to a space of their own

```bash
herdr-room out team --session roomlab
```

```
  run   herdr --session roomlab worktree open --cwd /private/tmp/roomlab/team \
          --path /private/tmp/roomlab/team/wt/member-a --label member-a --no-focus
  name  w6:p1 = desk
  name  w7:p1 = member-a
  name  w8:p1 = member-b
  the room space closed itself once empty · `herdr-room in team` rebuilds it
```

Out moves each pane to a new space, then runs `worktree open` for each worktree member after all the moves, so they nest under the repo again.

```
$ herdr --session roomlab workspace list | jq '[space, label, linked worktree]'
w6  desk      false
w7  member-a  true
w8  member-b  true
```

`out <room> <member>` moves only that member out; `out <room>` with no names moves everyone, the desk included.

chunks.title: 6. Rebuild the same room
chunks.label: One room, many agents: herdr-room in / out · 6. Rebuild the same room
chunks.text:
## 6. Rebuild the same room

```bash
herdr-room in team --session roomlab      # no members: use the saved state
```

```
room 'team' · session roomlab · layout fib · 3 members: desk, member-a, member-b
  name  w9:p1 = desk
  name  w9:p2 = member-a
  name  w9:p3 = member-b
```

chunks.title: 7. Room in with plain herdr
chunks.label: One room, many agents: herdr-room in / out · 7. Room in with plain herdr
chunks.text:
## 7. Room in with plain herdr

Every `run` line herdr-room prints is an ordinary `herdr pane move`. Without herdr-room you can do it by hand: move the pane into the room's tab, split beside a target pane, and give the share the target keeps.

```bash
herdr --session roomlab pane move <member-b> --tab <room tab> \
  --target-pane <desk> --split right --ratio 0.5 --no-focus
```

```
{"type":"pane_move","changed":null}
w9:p1  desk
w9:p5  member-b
w9:p4  member-a
```

Only `right` and `down` exist as split directions. If a move drops the agent's name, set it again with `herdr agent rename`.

chunks.title: 8. The trap: a new body starts while the old one is still in the room
chunks.label: One room, many agents: herdr-room in / out · 8. The trap: a new body starts while the old one is still in the room
chunks.text:
## 8. The trap: a new body starts while the old one is still in the room

The real case, 31 Oct: an agent moved its "body" (its pane) to another checkout. The old body opened a new pane and set a timer to close itself; before it closed, room in ran, and the room got an extra column. Reproduced:

```bash
herdr --session roomlab pane split <member-a> --direction down \
  --cwd /tmp/roomlab/team/wt/member-a --no-focus     # new body w9:p4, old body w9:p2 still there
herdr-room in team desk member-a-new member-b --layout fib --session roomlab
```

```
room 'team' · session roomlab · layout fib · 4 members: desk, member-a, member-b, member-a
  name  w9:p4 = member-a   (not an agent: skipped)
  name  w9:p2 = member-a
  rect  w9:p3    x=57   y=23  28x23
  rect  w9:p2    x=85   y=23  28x23
```

Three asked for, four in the room: **an open room keeps every pane already inside its space**, named or not. Editing the state file does not help: `in` builds the member list from the panes really in the space; the state only orders them.

The fix: the old body leaves first, then room in.

```bash
herdr --session roomlab pane close <old member-a>
herdr-room in team desk member-a-new member-b --layout fib --session roomlab
```

```
room 'team' · session roomlab · layout fib · 3 members: desk, member-a, member-b
  rect  w9:p1    x=0    y=0   57x46
  rect  w9:p4    x=57   y=0   56x23
  rect  w9:p3    x=57   y=23  56x23
```

chunks.title: 9. Rules the teams learned in real use
chunks.label: One room, many agents: herdr-room in / out · 9. Rules the teams learned in real use
chunks.text:
## 9. Rules the teams learned in real use

- **Only the desk runs in/out**; members use `--dry` only (27 Oct: two agents ran out at once and pane ids changed mid-way).
- **`--dry` first, every time**, then read the new pane ids from `herdr agent list` after every move and tell the team.
- **Move members while they are idle.** A busy agent is not restarted, but whoever watches it gets lost.
- **One plain space per repo** (main's). If another space whose cwd is inside the same repo comes first in the sidebar, out nests the worktrees under it instead. Fix: in, close the extra space (without `--group`, which would close the worktree's space too), out again.
- **Moving a body**: new body up first, old body leaves the space, wait until `agent list` no longer shows it, then in, then tell everyone the new pane ids.
- **Panes cannot cross sessions.** To move an agent to another session, resume its conversation in a new pane there instead.

chunks.title: 10. Install it yourself (everything is on this page)
chunks.label: One room, many agents: herdr-room in / out · 10. Install it yourself (everything is on this page)
chunks.text:
## 10. Install it yourself (everything is on this page)

You need:
- herdr 0.9.5 or later from [herdr.dev](https://herdr.dev) (this lesson ran on 0.9.5)
- python3 (standard library only: json, os, re, subprocess, sys, time) and git
- `jq` and `rg` are used only in the example commands and [`captures/capture.sh`](captures/capture.sh), not by the tool

Steps:

1. Save the source in section 11 as `~/.local/bin/herdr-room` and `chmod +x ~/.local/bin/herdr-room` (the same file is [`code/herdr-room`](code/herdr-room)).
2. If you use Claude Code, save the skill in section 12 as `~/.claude/skills/herdr-room/SKILL.md` (or [`code/SKILL.md`](code/SKILL.md)); the agent then knows when to call it.
3. Check: `herdr-room --help` prints the `herdr-room in <room> ...` line, and `herdr-room list` runs (no rooms is not an error).
4. Try it in a scratch session first, never on a room people are working in: open `herdr session attach roomlab` in one pane and follow sections 2 to 8, or run [`captures/capture.sh`](captures/capture.sh) whole. It does not create the test repo; make one with `git init` and two `git worktree add` as in section 2.
5. State lives in `~/.local/state/herdr-room/`; delete a room's file when you no longer need that room. To uninstall, delete the two files from steps 1-2.

The files here match the ones in daily use line for line, except 4 example paths rewritten as `~/Code/github.com/...`. The copy in this lesson runs:

```
$ python3 code/herdr-room list | rg roomlab   # the copy in this lesson, not the installed one
roomlab      team             fib   OPEN  desk · member-a · member-b   (saved 2026-10-31T21:02:03+0700)
```

chunks.title: 12. The full skill (`~/.claude/skills/herdr-room/SKILL.md`)
chunks.label: One room, many agents: herdr-room in / out · 12. The full skill (`~/.claude/skills/herdr-room/SKILL.md`)
chunks.text:
## 12. The full skill (`~/.claude/skills/herdr-room/SKILL.md`)

~~~~markdown
---
name: herdr-room
description: Pull live agents into one room (a herdr space whose single tab shows them all, fib/cols/rows/main layout) and send them back to spaces of their own, back and forth as often as you like, with no restart — real panes move and the member list is saved so `in` rebuilds the same room. Works from any pane in any session. Use when the user says "war room", "bring them into one room", "put X Y Z on one page", "send them back to their own spaces", "back and forth", "team page", "herdr-room", or wants a group view of several oracles and then their own spaces again. Do NOT use to start new agents from a charter (use /herdr-team), to move an agent between herdr sessions (panes cannot cross sessions — use the resume pattern in /herdr-bring), or to list where an oracle runs (use /herdr-info).
argument-hint: "in <room> [member…] [--layout fib|cols|rows|main] [--session S] [--dry] | out <room> [member…] [--session S] [--dry] | rename <room> <new> | list"
---

# /herdr-room — one page for a team, then back to their own spaces

Script: `~/.local/bin/herdr-room` (python3, calls `herdr --session S pane move` with exact pane ids).

```bash
herdr-room in  war-room ~/Code/github.com/Soul-Brews-Studio/kvmbox-oracle \
                        ~/Code/github.com/Soul-Brews-Studio/vpskeeper-oracle \
                        ~/Code/github.com/laris-co/gateway-oracle \
               --layout fib --session homekeeper --dry          # plan first, always
herdr-room out war-room --session homekeeper                     # each back to a space of its own
herdr-room out war-room vpskeeper-oracle --session homekeeper    # split: only that one leaves
herdr-room in  war-room --session homekeeper                     # rebuild the same room from saved state
herdr-room in  war-room /path/to/another-oracle --session homekeeper   # add a member: joins at the end
herdr-room in  war-room --layout cols --session homekeeper       # re-tile the open room
herdr-room list                                                  # saved rooms, OPEN or out
herdr-room rename war-room ops --session homekeeper             # space label + tab label + saved state
```

## Members
- An **agent name** (herdr-team names every member), a **folder name** (`gateway-oracle`), a
  **folder path** (the agent's cwd), or a **pane id** in that session. Prefer names and folders:
  pane ids repeat across herdr sessions (`w8:p2` was both office and war-room on 2026-10-05).
- A path matching several agents in one session is refused with the candidates; pass the pane id.
- A member found only in another session is refused with that session's name. Panes cannot cross
  herdr sessions; move the agent first (new pane waits for the old pid, then resumes — /herdr-bring).

## Layouts — the share is set inside each move (no resize afterwards, so no extra redraw)
| layout | shape |
|---|---|
| `fib` (default) | first member the left half; each next takes half of what is left, turning right/down (3: left · top-right · bottom-right; 4: … · bottom-right splits into two) |
| `cols` / `rows` | equal columns / rows in member order |
| `main` | first member a left column of share `--ratio` (default 0.5), the rest stacked right |

## How it moves (why it works from anywhere)
1. The first member opens the room: `pane move --new-workspace --label <room>` (or is already in it).
2. Every other member goes to a scratch tab in the room's space. Inside one space a pane keeps its id.
3. Each comes back into the main tab with `--split` and `--ratio` = the share the TARGET keeps.
   The scratch tab closes itself when empty; so does any space a member left empty.
4. Every member is renamed (herdr drops an agent's name on a move); shells are skipped.

`out` sends each member to a space labelled with its name (its existing space if one has that label),
saves the order and layout, and the room closes itself once empty.

**Worktree members are nested again** (fixed 2026-10-06). Sidebar nesting under the repo comes from a
flag on the SPACE (`worktree_space`), which only `herdr worktree create/open` sets. A plain
`pane move --new-workspace` gives a flat space, which is how the floodboy room broke out into 5 flat
spaces. `out` now:
1. Sends a member whose cwd is a linked git worktree back to the space that still holds that worktree,
   if any (a helper pane can keep the old worktree space alive). Otherwise it makes a new space.
2. After **all** moves, runs `herdr worktree open --cwd <repo> --path <wt> --label <name> --no-focus`
   for each worktree member. On a space already at that path it attaches the identity in place
   (`already_open: true`; no pane moves, the agent is untouched).

Order matters: an early `worktree open`, run while the room still exists, attached to the room, which
then closed. In the test the first member came out flat and the last one nested.

## With /herdr-team (split a team into spaces, merge it back)
/herdr-team starts a team in ONE space — the worktree's own space, Fibonacci, every member named.
That space is a room like any other:

```bash
herdr-room out <team-space> omp-rain omx-wind --session laris-co   # those two get spaces of their own
herdr-room in  <team-space> --session laris-co                      # back into the team's page
```

- Name the members to split. `out` with no members moves EVERYONE, the lead's pane included.
- A herdr space is not a git worktree: split members still share the worktree's folder and files.
  For a member with its own branch and folder, start it with /herdr-wt instead (a running agent
  cannot change its folder).

## Moving a body (an agent's pane moves to another checkout) — order matters
Met 2026-10-31 in laris-co room `aiexpo-oracle` (wCC): the old body (wCC:p3, a course-team worktree)
split a new pane down with cwd = the main checkout, started `claude` there, and set timers to
`/exit` + `pane close` itself 20-40 s later. The new body ran `herdr-room in` at 20:05:38, before
the old pane had gone: 3 members, 3 columns. A second `in` at 20:06:04, after the close: 2.
Reproduced on fake agents (`pane report-agent`) in a scratch session; proof book
`Caeruleus-Lab/aiexpo-oracle` `ψ/writing/proof-books/2026-10-31_herdr-body-move/` (commit 5124342).

1. New pane in the room's space, cwd = the new checkout; start the new body there with a brief.
2. The OLD body leaves the space: `herdr pane close <old>`, or `herdr-room out <room> <old> --dry`
   first (out also runs `worktree open` for a worktree member, giving it a space of its own).
3. Wait until `herdr agent list` no longer shows the old pane. Never on a timer you only hope fired.
4. Only now: `herdr-room in <room> <new> <peer> --layout <x> --session <s>`, then `herdr-room list`.
5. Tell the peers the new pane id (ids change on every move).

## State
`~/.local/state/herdr-room/<session>__<room>.json` — members (path, last pane id, name), layout, time.

## Traps (met 2026-10-05)
| trap | handled |
|---|---|
| `maw herdr join` from another session: "pane … not found" (it fills the tab of the pane it runs in) | herdr-room never uses "the pane I run in" |
| same pane id in two sessions → maw refuses as ambiguous, even with `--session` | members by path |
| agent name lost after a move or a swap | renamed after every move |
| moving into a zoomed tab returns `changed:false` silently | unzoom first (not automated yet) |
| a re-layout that resizes afterwards makes every agent redraw twice | shares set inside the moves |
| `out` gave worktree agents FLAT spaces, not nested under their repo (2026-10-06) | `worktree open` per worktree member, after all moves |
| `worktree open` while the room is alive attaches to the room (first member flat) | runs only after every move |
| `pane move --split left` → `invalid split direction` | only `right` / `down` exist |
| `pane move` into an existing space: the result has no `pane` key | look the pane up by `agent list` |
| `in` on an OPEN room keeps every pane already inside its space, typed or not (2026-10-31: the old body was still in the space, so `in <new> <wt>` gave 3 columns) | by design (`if ws:` branch, ~line 235): the old pane must LEAVE first. See "Moving a body" above |
| editing the state file to drop a member does nothing while the room is open | members are rebuilt from the panes in the space; the state only orders them |
| two agents moving or renaming at once: pane ids change mid-check (nsm 10-08, neo 10-11, relic4-scan 10-31) | only the desk runs `in`/`out`; everyone else `--dry` |
| `out` nested the worktree member under the WRONG parent: a second plain space whose cwd was inside the same repo (a capture space at `ψ/writing/proof-books/...`, label `proof-book`) came first in the sidebar, and `worktree open` linked the wt to it (2026-10-31) | keep ONE plain space per repo (the main oracle's). Close any extra space in that repo before `out`. If it already happened: `in` (frees the link), `workspace close <extra>` (without `--group`, which would close the wt's space too), `out` again |
| `workspace close` on that extra space: `workspace_group_close_required` | it now owns the linked wt; `--group` closes the wt agent's space as well. Room `in` first, then close |
| `herdr-room list` shows OPEN after `out` | the main oracle's own space carries the room's label; harmless (`in` uses it), but `list` cannot tell out from open |

Proven on throwaway shells in session laris-co (2026-10-05): fib 3 → out → in from state → add a 4th
(fib spiral 88x44 | 88x22 / 44x22 · 44x22) → cols → out → all spaces closed.
Proven on throwaway **worktrees** in session ccdc (2026-10-06): 2 linked worktrees → in → out → both
`WT` (nested); before the order fix it gave `t-a FLAT, t-b WT`. The 2026-10-05 tests used plain shells
only, which is why the worktree case slipped through. Test with worktrees whenever members can be worktrees.
~~~~

chunks.text:
## 1. ห้อง (room) คืออะไร

herdr เรียงของจากนอกเข้าใน: session > space (CLI เรียก workspace) > tab > pane > agent

**ห้อง** คือ space หนึ่งที่ tab เดียวโชว์ agent หลายตัวพร้อมกัน เช่นโต๊ะทีม (desk) ซ้าย สมาชิกขวา `herdr-room` ย้าย pane จริง ไม่เปิด agent ใหม่ จึงย้ายไปกลับกี่รอบก็ได้

```
$ herdr-room --help | head -8
  herdr-room in  <room> [member ...] [--layout fib|cols|rows|main] [--ratio R] [--session S] [--dry]
  herdr-room out <room> [member ...] [--session S] [--dry]   (members given: only they leave)
  herdr-room list
  herdr-room rename <room> <new-name> [--session S]   (space label, tab label and saved state)
```

chunks.title: 2. เตรียมทีม: main 1 space + worktree ละ space
chunks.label: ห้องเดียว หลาย agent: herdr-room in / out · 2. เตรียมทีม: main 1 space + worktree ละ space
chunks.text:
## 2. เตรียมทีม: main 1 space + worktree ละ space

space ของ main สร้างด้วย `workspace create` ส่วน worktree ต้องเปิดด้วย `worktree open` เพราะ herdr จะซ้อน space ไว้ใต้ repo ใน sidebar ก็ต่อเมื่อ space นั้นผูกกับ worktree

```bash
herdr --session roomlab workspace create --cwd /tmp/roomlab/team --label desk --no-focus
herdr --session roomlab worktree open --cwd /tmp/roomlab/team \
  --path /tmp/roomlab/team/wt/member-a --label member-a --no-focus
```

```
{"space":"w2","pane":"w2:p1"}
{"space":"w3","label":"member-a","linked":true}

## 9. กฎที่ทีมได้มาจากการใช้จริง

- **desk คนเดียวเป็นคนสั่ง in/out** สมาชิกใช้แค่ `--dry` (27 ต.ค. มี agent สองตัวสั่ง out พร้อมกัน pane id เปลี่ยนกลางทาง)

- **ย้ายตอนสมาชิกว่าง** ย้ายตอนกำลังรันงานยาวไม่ restart ก็จริง แต่คนดูจะงง
- **repo หนึ่งมี space ธรรมดาแค่อันเดียว** (ของ main) ถ้ามี space อื่นที่ cwd อยู่ใน repo เดียวกันขึ้นมาก่อนใน sidebar ตอน out worktree จะไปซ้อนใต้ space นั้นแทน แก้โดย in ก่อน ปิด space เกิน (ไม่ใช้ `--group` ซึ่งจะปิด space ของ worktree ไปด้วย) แล้ว out ใหม่

chunks.text:
## 12. skill เต็ม (`~/.claude/skills/herdr-room/SKILL.md`)

~~~~markdown
---
name: herdr-room
description: Pull live agents into one room (a herdr space whose single tab shows them all, fib/cols/rows/main layout) and send them back to spaces of their own, back and forth as often as you like, with no restart — real panes move and the member list is saved so `in` rebuilds the same room. Works from any pane in any session. Use when the user says "war room", "bring them into one room", "put X Y Z on one page", "send them back to their own spaces", "back and forth", "team page", "herdr-room", or wants a group view of several oracles and then their own spaces again. Do NOT use to start new agents from a charter (use /herdr-team), to move an agent between herdr sessions (panes cannot cross sessions — use the resume pattern in /herdr-bring), or to list where an oracle runs (use /herdr-info).
argument-hint: "in <room> [member…] [--layout fib|cols|rows|main] [--session S] [--dry] | out <room> [member…] [--session S] [--dry] | rename <room> <new> | list"
---

# /herdr-room — one page for a team, then back to their own spaces

Script: `~/.local/bin/herdr-room` (python3, calls `herdr --session S pane move` with exact pane ids).

```bash
herdr-room in  war-room ~/Code/github.com/Soul-Brews-Studio/kvmbox-oracle \
                        ~/Code/github.com/Soul-Brews-Studio/vpskeeper-oracle \
                        ~/Code/github.com/laris-co/gateway-oracle \
               --layout fib --session homekeeper --dry          # plan first, always
herdr-room out war-room --session homekeeper                     # each back to a space of its own
herdr-room out war-room vpskeeper-oracle --session homekeeper    # split: only that one leaves
herdr-room in  war-room --session homekeeper                     # rebuild the same room from saved state
herdr-room in  war-room /path/to/another-oracle --session homekeeper   # add a member: joins at the end
herdr-room in  war-room --layout cols --session homekeeper       # re-tile the open room
herdr-room list                                                  # saved rooms, OPEN or out
herdr-room rename war-room ops --session homekeeper             # space label + tab label + saved state
```

## Members
- An **agent name** (herdr-team names every member), a **folder name** (`gateway-oracle`), a
  **folder path** (the agent's cwd), or a **pane id** in that session. Prefer names and folders:
  pane ids repeat across herdr sessions (`w8:p2` was both office and war-room on 2026-10-05).
- A path matching several agents in one session is refused with the candidates; pass the pane id.
- A member found only in another session is refused with that session's name. Panes cannot cross
  herdr sessions; move the agent first (new pane waits for the old pid, then resumes — /herdr-bring).

## Layouts — the share is set inside each move (no resize afterwards, so no extra redraw)
| layout | shape |
|---|---|
| `fib` (default) | first member the left half; each next takes half of what is left, turning right/down (3: left · top-right · bottom-right; 4: … · bottom-right splits into two) |
| `cols` / `rows` | equal columns / rows in member order |
| `main` | first member a left column of share `--ratio` (default 0.5), the rest stacked right |

## How it moves (why it works from anywhere)
1. The first member opens the room: `pane move --new-workspace --label <room>` (or is already in it).
2. Every other member goes to a scratch tab in the room's space. Inside one space a pane keeps its id.
3. Each comes back into the main tab with `--split` and `--ratio` = the share the TARGET keeps.
   The scratch tab closes itself when empty; so does any space a member left empty.
4. Every member is renamed (herdr drops an agent's name on a move); shells are skipped.

`out` sends each member to a space labelled with its name (its existing space if one has that label),
saves the order and layout, and the room closes itself once empty.

**Worktree members are nested again** (fixed 2026-10-06). Sidebar nesting under the repo comes from a
flag on the SPACE (`worktree_space`), which only `herdr worktree create/open` sets. A plain
`pane move --new-workspace` gives a flat space, which is how the floodboy room broke out into 5 flat
spaces. `out` now:
1. Sends a member whose cwd is a linked git worktree back to the space that still holds that worktree,
   if any (a helper pane can keep the old worktree space alive). Otherwise it makes a new space.
2. After **all** moves, runs `herdr worktree open --cwd <repo> --path <wt> --label <name> --no-focus`
   for each worktree member. On a space already at that path it attaches the identity in place
   (`already_open: true`; no pane moves, the agent is untouched).

Order matters: an early `worktree open`, run while the room still exists, attached to the room, which
then closed. In the test the first member came out flat and the last one nested.

## With /herdr-team (split a team into spaces, merge it back)
/herdr-team starts a team in ONE space — the worktree's own space, Fibonacci, every member named.
That space is a room like any other:

```bash
herdr-room out <team-space> omp-rain omx-wind --session laris-co   # those two get spaces of their own
herdr-room in  <team-space> --session laris-co                      # back into the team's page
```

- Name the members to split. `out` with no members moves EVERYONE, the lead's pane included.
- A herdr space is not a git worktree: split members still share the worktree's folder and files.
  For a member with its own branch and folder, start it with /herdr-wt instead (a running agent
  cannot change its folder).

## Moving a body (an agent's pane moves to another checkout) — order matters
Met 2026-10-31 in laris-co room `aiexpo-oracle` (wCC): the old body (wCC:p3, a course-team worktree)
split a new pane down with cwd = the main checkout, started `claude` there, and set timers to
`/exit` + `pane close` itself 20-40 s later. The new body ran `herdr-room in` at 20:05:38, before
the old pane had gone: 3 members, 3 columns. A second `in` at 20:06:04, after the close: 2.
Reproduced on fake agents (`pane report-agent`) in a scratch session; proof book
`Caeruleus-Lab/aiexpo-oracle` `ψ/writing/proof-books/2026-10-31_herdr-body-move/` (commit 5124342).

1. New pane in the room's space, cwd = the new checkout; start the new body there with a brief.
2. The OLD body leaves the space: `herdr pane close <old>`, or `herdr-room out <room> <old> --dry`
   first (out also runs `worktree open` for a worktree member, giving it a space of its own).
3. Wait until `herdr agent list` no longer shows the old pane. Never on a timer you only hope fired.
4. Only now: `herdr-room in <room> <new> <peer> --layout <x> --session <s>`, then `herdr-room list`.
5. Tell the peers the new pane id (ids change on every move).

## State
`~/.local/state/herdr-room/<session>__<room>.json` — members (path, last pane id, name), layout, time.

## Traps (met 2026-10-05)
| trap | handled |
|---|---|
| `maw herdr join` from another session: "pane … not found" (it fills the tab of the pane it runs in) | herdr-room never uses "the pane I run in" |
| same pane id in two sessions → maw refuses as ambiguous, even with `--session` | members by path |
| agent name lost after a move or a swap | renamed after every move |
| moving into a zoomed tab returns `changed:false` silently | unzoom first (not automated yet) |
| a re-layout that resizes afterwards makes every agent redraw twice | shares set inside the moves |
| `out` gave worktree agents FLAT spaces, not nested under their repo (2026-10-06) | `worktree open` per worktree member, after all moves |
| `worktree open` while the room is alive attaches to the room (first member flat) | runs only after every move |
| `pane move --split left` → `invalid split direction` | only `right` / `down` exist |
| `pane move` into an existing space: the result has no `pane` key | look the pane up by `agent list` |
| `in` on an OPEN room keeps every pane already inside its space, typed or not (2026-10-31: the old body was still in the space, so `in <new> <wt>` gave 3 columns) | by design (`if ws:` branch, ~line 235): the old pane must LEAVE first. See "Moving a body" above |
| editing the state file to drop a member does nothing while the room is open | members are rebuilt from the panes in the space; the state only orders them |
| two agents moving or renaming at once: pane ids change mid-check (nsm 10-08, neo 10-11, relic4-scan 10-31) | only the desk runs `in`/`out`; everyone else `--dry` |
| `out` nested the worktree member under the WRONG parent: a second plain space whose cwd was inside the same repo (a capture space at `ψ/writing/proof-books/...`, label `proof-book`) came first in the sidebar, and `worktree open` linked the wt to it (2026-10-31) | keep ONE plain space per repo (the main oracle's). Close any extra space in that repo before `out`. If it already happened: `in` (frees the link), `workspace close <extra>` (without `--group`, which would close the wt's space too), `out` again |
| `workspace close` on that extra space: `workspace_group_close_required` | it now owns the linked wt; `--group` closes the wt agent's space as well. Room `in` first, then close |
| `herdr-room list` shows OPEN after `out` | the main oracle's own space carries the room's label; harmless (`in` uses it), but `list` cannot tell out from open |

Proven on throwaway shells in session laris-co (2026-10-05): fib 3 → out → in from state → add a 4th
(fib spiral 88x44 | 88x22 / 44x22 · 44x22) → cols → out → all spaces closed.
Proven on throwaway **worktrees** in session ccdc (2026-10-06): 2 linked worktrees → in → out → both
`WT` (nested); before the order fix it gave `t-a FLAT, t-b WT`. The 2026-10-05 tests used plain shells
only, which is why the worktree case slipped through. Test with worktrees whenever members can be worktrees.
~~~~

chunks.title: 1. What MCP is
chunks.label: Build your own MCP: turn lessons into tools for AI · 1. What MCP is
chunks.text:
## 1. What MCP is

MCP (Model Context Protocol) is a common language between an AI and tools. The side the AI lives on is the client (claude.ai, ChatGPT, Claude Code, Codex); the side with the tools is the server.

- Every message is JSON-RPC 2.0: `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"...","params":{...}}`
- A server that only offers tools needs to answer three methods:
  - `initialize`: the client says hello; the server answers with its name, version and that it has tools
  - `tools/list`: which tools exist and what input each takes (JSON Schema)
  - `tools/call`: run a tool; the answer is `content`, as text or images
- A message without an `id` is a notification, e.g. `notifications/initialized`; the server does not answer it.
- Two ways to carry the messages (transports):
  - **stdio**: the client starts the server as a child process, writes one JSON per line to stdin and reads answers from stdout
  - **Streamable HTTP**: the client POSTs JSON to one URL, such as `/mcp`, and gets JSON back

## 4. Connect mini-mcp to Claude Code

Write a config that tells the client how to start the server, then let Claude use the tool:

```json
{"mcpServers":{"mini":{"command":"node","args":["mini-mcp.mjs"]}}}
```

```
$ claude -p --mcp-config mini.json --allowedTools mcp__mini__search "..."
`/rrr` writes the retrospective. The search returned the note's title, `rrr`, but no separate note id, so `rrr` is the closest identifier I have.
(exit 0)
```

To keep it, register it once: `claude mcp add mini -- node /path/to/mini-mcp.mjs`. In Claude Code the tool is named `mcp__<server>__<tool>`, e.g. `mcp__mini__search`.

chunks.title: 5. The data: cutting lessons into chunks (build_chunks.py)
chunks.label: Build your own MCP: turn lessons into tools for AI · 5. The data: cutting lessons into chunks (build_chunks.py)
chunks.text:
## 5. The data: cutting lessons into chunks (build_chunks.py)

mini-mcp searches four notes; the real one searches every lesson, Thai and English. The first job is to prepare the data ahead of time, not when someone asks.

`build_chunks.py` reads every lesson's README and:

1. Cuts at each `## ` heading, skipping lines inside code blocks (it counts ```` ``` ```` open and close); otherwise a `## ` comment in code becomes a fake heading.
2. Tags topics (install, skill, browser, ...) from words in the title and text.
3. Embeds each chunk with Workers AI `@cf/baai/bge-m3` (multilingual, Thai OK, 1024 dims), only for chunks whose text changed.
4. Stores the screenshots as base64 in `images.json` (max 1280 px, JPEG 80), so the server can show them to the AI.

One chunk:

```
$ jq '.chunks[] | select(.id=="herdr-room/th/5") | {id, lesson, lang, title, url, text: .text[0:120], vec: (.vec|length)}' chunks.json
{
  "id": "herdr-room/th/5",
  "lesson": "herdr-room",
  "lang": "th",
  "title": "5. room out: ทุกคนกลับ space ของตัวเอง",
  "url": "https://aiexpo.buildwithoracle.com/2026-10-31_herdr-room-lesson/th#s6",
  "text": "## 5. room out: ทุกคนกลับ space ของตัวเอง\n\n```bash\nherdr-room out team --session roomlab\n```\n\n```\n  run   herdr --sessio",
  "vec": 1024
}
(exit 0)
```

`url` points at `#s6` on the web page, so a search hit takes a person straight to that section. That is why section ids on the page must never shift: a section added in front gets its own id and the old ones stay.

## 7. Talk to the Cloudflare MCP with curl

No client needed to test it; POST the JSON yourself:

```
$ curl -s -X POST $M -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{initialize}' | jq '.result | {protocolVersion, serverInfo}'
{
  "protocolVersion": "2025-06-18",
  "serverInfo": {
    "name": "aiexpo-lessons",
    "title": "AIExpo Oracle lessons",
    "version": "2026.10.30-3"
  },
  "capabilities": {
    "tools": {
      "listChanged": false
    }
  }
}
(exit 0)
```

```
$ curl ... -d '{tools/list}' | jq -r '.result.tools[] | .name + ": " + .description[0:70]'
search: Search the AIExpo Oracle workshop lessons (Thai and English): installi
fetch: Read the full text of a search result. id '<lesson>/<lang>/<section>' 
get_image: Return screenshots as images the model can see. id is an image id from
list_lessons: List every lesson in workshop order, with page URLs, language editions
(exit 0)
```

Search in Thai, Thai edition only:

```
$ curl ... -d '{tools/call search {query: "ห้องเดียว หลาย agent", lang: th}}' | jq -r '.result.content[0].text | fromjson | .results[] | .id + "  " + .title' | head -3
herdr-room/th/1  ห้องเดียว หลาย agent: herdr-room in / out · 1. ห้อง (room) คืออะไร
herdr-room/th/8  ห้องเดียว หลาย agent: herdr-room in / out · 8. กับดัก: ร่างใหม่เกิดขณะร่างเก่ายังอยู่ในห้อง
herdr-room/th/9  ห้องเดียว หลาย agent: herdr-room in / out · 9. กฎที่ทีมได้มาจากการใช้จริง
(exit 0)
```

Read a whole section by the id search returned:

```
$ curl ... -d '{tools/call fetch {id: "mcp-connect/en/2"}}' | jq -r '.result.content[0].text | fromjson | .text' | head -8
## 2. claude.ai

**2.1 Add a connector.** Go to **Customize → Connectors**, press **Add**, then **Add custom connector**.

![Customize, Connectors tab, with the Add menu open showing Add custom connector](https://aiexpo.buildwithoracle.com/2026-10-30_mcp-connect-guide/images/01-claude-add-connector-menu.png)

**2.2 Name and URL.** Any name, for example `AIExpo lessons`, and the URL `https://aiexpo.buildwithoracle.com/mcp`. Press **Continue**.

(exit 0)
```

The names `search` and `fetch`, and the result shape (`results[]` with `id title url`), follow what ChatGPT connectors and deep research require, so the same server works for both claude.ai and ChatGPT (how to connect: the lesson [Connect claude.ai and ChatGPT to the lessons MCP](../2026-10-30_mcp-connect-guide/en)).

chunks.title: 8. Deploy to Cloudflare
chunks.label: Build your own MCP: turn lessons into tools for AI · 8. Deploy to Cloudflare
chunks.text:
## 8. Deploy to Cloudflare

```
$ cat wrangler.jsonc
// The lessons as a Worker on aiexpo.buildwithoracle.com: static assets, plus a read-only MCP endpoint at /mcp (worker.js, hybrid search over chunks.json with Workers AI bge-m3).
// Deploy: ./deploy.sh  (copies only committed files into dist/, then wrangler deploy)
{
  "name": "aiexpo-lessons",
  "main": "worker.js",
  "compatibility_date": "2026-10-01",
  "account_id": "a5eabdc2b11aae9bd5af46bd6a88179e",
  "ai": { "binding": "AI" },
  "assets": { "directory": "./dist", "binding": "ASSETS", "html_handling": "auto-trailing-slash", "run_worker_first": ["/mcp", "/mcp/*", "/*/videos/*"] },
  "routes": [{ "pattern": "aiexpo.buildwithoracle.com", "custom_domain": true }]
}
(exit 0)
```

- `run_worker_first` lists the paths the Worker answers before the static files: `/mcp` must be in it, or the assets answer 404 before the code runs.
- `"ai": { "binding": "AI" }` lets the Worker call bge-m3 with `env.AI.run(...)`.
- `deploy.sh` copies only committed files (`git archive HEAD`) into `dist/`, then runs `wrangler deploy`, so uncommitted files never reach the site.

chunks.title: 9. The stdio copy from GitHub (server.mjs)
chunks.label: Build your own MCP: turn lessons into tools for AI · 9. The stdio copy from GitHub (server.mjs)
chunks.text:
## 9. The stdio copy from GitHub (server.mjs)

GitHub Pages serves files only and cannot answer a POST, so it cannot host an HTTP MCP. Instead the server runs on your machine and reads `lessons.json`, `chunks.json` and `images.json` from Pages ([code/server.mjs](code/server.mjs), 232 lines).

- `package.json` declares `"bin": { "aiexpo-lessons": "mcp/server.mjs" }`, so `npx -y github:<org>/<repo>` fetches the repo and runs the server, with nothing published to npm.
- Search is keyword only, because embedding the query needs bge-m3 on Cloudflare.
- Set `AIEXPO_DIR=/path/to/clone` to read the files from disk instead of the web, for offline use.

```
$ printf initialize + tools/call search {query: "herdr room out"} | npx -y github:Caeruleus-Lab/aiexpo-lessons
{"serverInfo":{"name":"aiexpo-lessons","title":"AIExpo Oracle lessons (GitHub copy)","version":"2026.10.31-1"}}
{"id":"herdr-room/en/5","title":"One room, many agents: herdr-room in / out · 5. Room out: everyone back to a space of their own"}
{"id":"herdr-room/en/11","title":"One room, many agents: herdr-room in / out · 11. Full source of `herdr-room` (449 lines, python3)"}
{"id":"herdr-room/en/12","title":"One room, many agents: herdr-room in / out · 12. The full skill (`~/.claude/skills/herdr-room/SKILL.md`)"}
(exit 0)
```

Register it in Claude Code: `claude mcp add aiexpo-github -- npx -y github:Caeruleus-Lab/aiexpo-lessons`

chunks.title: 11. Traps we really hit
chunks.label: Build your own MCP: turn lessons into tools for AI · 11. Traps we really hit
chunks.text:
## 11. Traps we really hit

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| A Python script gets 403 from `/mcp` | Cloudflare blocks the `Python-urllib` user agent | Send your own `User-Agent` header |
| `claude -p` says "Not logged in" | A new process does not get the main session's token | Pass `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` to it (we load it from an uncommitted `.envrc`) |
| `/mcp` answers 404 | The assets answer before the Worker | Put `/mcp` in `run_worker_first` |
| Thai search misses words that are there | Thai has no spaces; splitting on spaces fails | `Intl.Segmenter("th", { granularity: "word" })` |
| Fake headings in the chunks | `## ` inside a code block counted as a heading | Cut headings only outside ```` ``` ```` |
| Search links land on the wrong section | A section added in front shifted the ids | The new section gets its own id (`#watch`), so `#s2…` stay put |
| `get_image` returns an error | Wrong argument name | The argument is `id`; always read names from `tools/list` |

```
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -A 'Python-urllib/3.12' $M   # Cloudflare bot rule
Python-urllib UA: 403
browser UA:       200
(exit 0)
```

chunks.label: สร้าง MCP ของตัวเอง: จากบทเรียนเป็นเครื่องมือให้ AI · 1. MCP คืออะไร
chunks.text:
## 1. MCP คืออะไร

MCP (Model Context Protocol) คือภาษากลางระหว่าง AI กับเครื่องมือ ฝั่งที่ AI อยู่เรียกว่า client (claude.ai, ChatGPT, Claude Code, Codex) ฝั่งที่มีเครื่องมือเรียกว่า server

- ข้อความทุกอันเป็น JSON-RPC 2.0: `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"...","params":{...}}`
- server ที่มีแค่เครื่องมือ ตอบแค่สามคำสั่งก็พอ
  - `initialize`: client ทักทาย server ตอบชื่อ เวอร์ชัน และบอกว่ามี tools
  - `tools/list`: บอกว่ามีเครื่องมืออะไร แต่ละตัวรับ input หน้าตาแบบไหน (JSON Schema)
  - `tools/call`: เรียกเครื่องมือจริง ได้ `content` กลับมาเป็น text หรือ image
- ข้อความที่ไม่มี `id` คือ notification เช่น `notifications/initialized` server ไม่ต้องตอบ
- ส่งข้อความได้สองทาง (transport)
  - **stdio**: client เปิด server เป็นโปรเซสลูก ส่ง JSON บรรทัดละอันทาง stdin รับคำตอบทาง stdout
  - **Streamable HTTP**: client POST JSON ไปที่ URL เดียว เช่น `/mcp` ได้ JSON กลับมา

chunks.text:
## 5. ข้อมูล: ตัดบทเรียนเป็นชิ้น (build_chunks.py)

mini-mcp ค้นโน้ตสี่อัน ของจริงค้นบทเรียนทั้งหมด ไทยและอังกฤษ งานแรกคือเตรียมข้อมูลไว้ล่วงหน้า ไม่ใช่ทำตอนมีคนถาม

`build_chunks.py` อ่าน README ของทุกบทเรียน แล้ว:

1. ตัดที่หัวข้อ `## ` ทีละหัวข้อ แต่ข้ามบรรทัดที่อยู่ในบล็อกโค้ด (นับ ```` ``` ```` เปิดปิด) ไม่งั้นคอมเมนต์ `## ` ในโค้ดจะกลายเป็นหัวข้อปลอม
2. ติดป้าย topic (install, skill, browser, ...) ด้วยคำที่เจอในหัวข้อและเนื้อหา
3. ทำ vector ของแต่ละชิ้นด้วย Workers AI `@cf/baai/bge-m3` (หลายภาษา ไทยได้ 1024 มิติ) ทำใหม่เฉพาะชิ้นที่ข้อความเปลี่ยน
4. เก็บภาพหน้าจอเป็น base64 ลง `images.json` (ย่อไม่เกิน 1280 px, JPEG 80) ให้ server ส่งภาพให้ AI ดูได้

หน้าตาของหนึ่งชิ้น:

```
$ jq '.chunks[] | select(.id=="herdr-room/th/5") | {id, lesson, lang, title, url, text: .text[0:120], vec: (.vec|length)}' chunks.json
{
  "id": "herdr-room/th/5",
  "lesson": "herdr-room",
  "lang": "th",
  "title": "5. room out: ทุกคนกลับ space ของตัวเอง",
  "url": "https://aiexpo.buildwithoracle.com/2026-10-31_herdr-room-lesson/th#s6",
  "text": "## 5. room out: ทุกคนกลับ space ของตัวเอง\n\n```bash\nherdr-room out team --session roomlab\n```\n\n```\n  run   herdr --sessio",
  "vec": 1024
}
(exit 0)
```

`url` ชี้ไปที่ `#s6` ของหน้าเว็บ ลิงก์จากผลค้นจึงพาคนไปถึงหัวข้อนั้นตรง ๆ id ของหัวข้อในหน้าเว็บจึงห้ามเลื่อน ถ้าเพิ่ม section ข้างหน้า ต้องให้ id เดิมคงที่

chunks.title: 7. คุยกับ MCP บน Cloudflare ด้วย curl
chunks.label: สร้าง MCP ของตัวเอง: จากบทเรียนเป็นเครื่องมือให้ AI · 7. คุยกับ MCP บน Cloudflare ด้วย curl
chunks.text:
## 7. คุยกับ MCP บน Cloudflare ด้วย curl

ไม่ต้องมี client ก็ทดสอบได้ POST JSON ตรง ๆ:

```
$ curl -s -X POST $M -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{initialize}' | jq '.result | {protocolVersion, serverInfo}'
{
  "protocolVersion": "2025-06-18",
  "serverInfo": {
    "name": "aiexpo-lessons",
    "title": "AIExpo Oracle lessons",
    "version": "2026.10.30-3"
  },
  "capabilities": {
    "tools": {
      "listChanged": false
    }
  }
}
(exit 0)
```

```
$ curl ... -d '{tools/list}' | jq -r '.result.tools[] | .name + ": " + .description[0:70]'
search: Search the AIExpo Oracle workshop lessons (Thai and English): installi
fetch: Read the full text of a search result. id '<lesson>/<lang>/<section>' 
get_image: Return screenshots as images the model can see. id is an image id from
list_lessons: List every lesson in workshop order, with page URLs, language editions
(exit 0)
```

ค้นเป็นภาษาไทย กรองเฉพาะฉบับไทย:

```
$ curl ... -d '{tools/call search {query: "ห้องเดียว หลาย agent", lang: th}}' | jq -r '.result.content[0].text | fromjson | .results[] | .id + "  " + .title' | head -3
herdr-room/th/1  ห้องเดียว หลาย agent: herdr-room in / out · 1. ห้อง (room) คืออะไร
herdr-room/th/8  ห้องเดียว หลาย agent: herdr-room in / out · 8. กับดัก: ร่างใหม่เกิดขณะร่างเก่ายังอยู่ในห้อง
herdr-room/th/9  ห้องเดียว หลาย agent: herdr-room in / out · 9. กฎที่ทีมได้มาจากการใช้จริง
(exit 0)
```

อ่านเต็มหัวข้อด้วย id ที่ได้จาก search:

```
$ curl ... -d '{tools/call fetch {id: "mcp-connect/en/2"}}' | jq -r '.result.content[0].text | fromjson | .text' | head -8
## 2. claude.ai

**2.1 Add a connector.** Go to **Customize → Connectors**, press **Add**, then **Add custom connector**.

![Customize, Connectors tab, with the Add menu open showing Add custom connector](https://aiexpo.buildwithoracle.com/2026-10-30_mcp-connect-guide/images/01-claude-add-connector-menu.png)

**2.2 Name and URL.** Any name, for example `AIExpo lessons`, and the URL `https://aiexpo.buildwithoracle.com/mcp`. Press **Continue**.

(exit 0)
```

ชื่อ `search` กับ `fetch` และรูปร่างผลลัพธ์ (`results[]` ที่มี `id title url`) ตั้งตามที่ ChatGPT connector และ deep research ต้องการ ตัวเดียวกันจึงใช้ได้ทั้ง claude.ai และ ChatGPT (วิธีต่อ อยู่ในบทเรียน [ต่อ claude.ai และ ChatGPT เข้ากับ MCP](../2026-10-30_mcp-connect-guide/th))

chunks.title: 8. Deploy ขึ้น Cloudflare
chunks.label: สร้าง MCP ของตัวเอง: จากบทเรียนเป็นเครื่องมือให้ AI · 8. Deploy ขึ้น Cloudflare
chunks.text:
## 8. Deploy ขึ้น Cloudflare

```
$ cat wrangler.jsonc
// The lessons as a Worker on aiexpo.buildwithoracle.com: static assets, plus a read-only MCP endpoint at /mcp (worker.js, hybrid search over chunks.json with Workers AI bge-m3).
// Deploy: ./deploy.sh  (copies only committed files into dist/, then wrangler deploy)
{
  "name": "aiexpo-lessons",
  "main": "worker.js",
  "compatibility_date": "2026-10-01",
  "account_id": "a5eabdc2b11aae9bd5af46bd6a88179e",
  "ai": { "binding": "AI" },
  "assets": { "directory": "./dist", "binding": "ASSETS", "html_handling": "auto-trailing-slash", "run_worker_first": ["/mcp", "/mcp/*", "/*/videos/*"] },
  "routes": [{ "pattern": "aiexpo.buildwithoracle.com", "custom_domain": true }]
}
(exit 0)
```

- `run_worker_first` บอกว่า path ไหนให้ Worker ตอบก่อนไฟล์ static: `/mcp` ต้องอยู่ในนี้ ไม่งั้น assets จะตอบ 404 ก่อนถึงโค้ด
- `"ai": { "binding": "AI" }` ทำให้ `env.AI.run(...)` เรียก bge-m3 ได้จากใน Worker
- `deploy.sh` copy เฉพาะไฟล์ที่ commit แล้ว (`git archive HEAD`) ลง `dist/` แล้ว `wrangler deploy` ไฟล์ที่ยังไม่ commit จึงไม่หลุดขึ้นเว็บ

chunks.label: สร้าง MCP ของตัวเอง: จากบทเรียนเป็นเครื่องมือให้ AI · 9. ตัว stdio จาก GitHub (server.mjs)
chunks.text:
## 9. ตัว stdio จาก GitHub (server.mjs)

GitHub Pages เสิร์ฟได้แค่ไฟล์ ตอบ POST ไม่ได้ จึงเป็น MCP แบบ HTTP ไม่ได้ ทางออกคือให้ server รันในเครื่องเรา แล้วไปอ่าน `lessons.json` `chunks.json` `images.json` จาก Pages ([code/server.mjs](code/server.mjs) 232 บรรทัด)

- `package.json` ประกาศ `"bin": { "aiexpo-lessons": "mcp/server.mjs" }` คำสั่ง `npx -y github:<org>/<repo>` จึงดึง repo มารัน server ได้เลย ไม่ต้อง publish ขึ้น npm
- ค้นด้วยคำอย่างเดียว เพราะการแปลงคำถามเป็น vector ต้องใช้ bge-m3 บน Cloudflare
- ตั้ง `AIEXPO_DIR=/path/to/clone` ให้อ่านไฟล์จากดิสก์แทนเว็บได้ ใช้ offline ได้

```
$ printf initialize + tools/call search {query: "herdr room out"} | npx -y github:Caeruleus-Lab/aiexpo-lessons
{"serverInfo":{"name":"aiexpo-lessons","title":"AIExpo Oracle lessons (GitHub copy)","version":"2026.10.31-1"}}
{"id":"herdr-room/en/5","title":"One room, many agents: herdr-room in / out · 5. Room out: everyone back to a space of their own"}
{"id":"herdr-room/en/11","title":"One room, many agents: herdr-room in / out · 11. Full source of `herdr-room` (449 lines, python3)"}
{"id":"herdr-room/en/12","title":"One room, many agents: herdr-room in / out · 12. The full skill (`~/.claude/skills/herdr-room/SKILL.md`)"}
(exit 0)
```

ลงทะเบียนใน Claude Code: `claude mcp add aiexpo-github -- npx -y github:Caeruleus-Lab/aiexpo-lessons`

chunks.title: 11. กับดักที่เจอจริง
chunks.label: สร้าง MCP ของตัวเอง: จากบทเรียนเป็นเครื่องมือให้ AI · 11. กับดักที่เจอจริง
chunks.text:
## 11. กับดักที่เจอจริง

| อาการ | สาเหตุ | ทางแก้ |
|---|---|---|
| สคริปต์ Python เรียก `/mcp` ได้ 403 | Cloudflare บล็อก user agent `Python-urllib` | ส่ง header `User-Agent` ของตัวเอง |
| `claude -p` ตอบ "Not logged in" | โปรเซสใหม่ไม่ได้ token ที่ session หลักใช้ | ส่ง `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` ให้โปรเซสนั้น (เราโหลดจาก `.envrc` ที่ไม่ commit) |
| `/mcp` ตอบ 404 | assets ตอบก่อน Worker | ใส่ `/mcp` ใน `run_worker_first` |
| ผลค้นภาษาไทยไม่เจอคำที่มีอยู่จริง | ภาษาไทยไม่มีช่องว่าง ตัดด้วย space ไม่ได้ | `Intl.Segmenter("th", { granularity: "word" })` |
| หัวข้อปลอมโผล่ใน chunks | `## ` ในบล็อกโค้ดถูกนับเป็นหัวข้อ | ตัดหัวข้อเฉพาะนอก ```` ``` ```` |
| ลิงก์จากผลค้นพาไปผิดหัวข้อ | เพิ่ม section ไว้หน้าบทเรียน id เลื่อน | section ใหม่ใช้ id ของตัวเอง (`#watch`) ให้ `#s2…` คงที่ |
| `get_image` ได้ error | ส่ง argument ชื่อผิด | argument ชื่อ `id` ดูชื่อจาก `tools/list` ทุกครั้ง |

```
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -A 'Python-urllib/3.12' $M   # Cloudflare bot rule
Python-urllib UA: 403
browser UA:       200
(exit 0)
```

chunks.title: 1. What the Antigravity CLI is
chunks.label: Use the Antigravity CLI (agy) with the lessons MCP · 1. What the Antigravity CLI is

images.alt: Summary card: two MCP servers added to agy, agy mcp list shows both enabled, agy -p answers through aiexpo-github with 7 lessons, and the three traps at sign-in and add

chunks.text:
## 1. What the Antigravity CLI is

The Antigravity CLI is Google's coding agent for the terminal; the command is `agy`. It uses the Gemini model of the signed-in account (on this machine: Google AI Pro, model "Gemini 4 Argon (Medium)").

- **The Antigravity desktop app (2.3.1) does not ship the `agy` command.** The CLI is a separate install.
- `agy` connects to MCP servers of both kinds: `http` (a URL) and `stdio` (a command run on your machine).

```
$ agy --version
1.4.12
(exit 0)
```

![Summary card: two MCP servers added to agy, agy mcp list shows both enabled, agy -p answers through aiexpo-github with 7 lessons, and the three traps at sign-in and add](images/01-agy-mcp.png)

chunks.title: 2. Install
chunks.label: Use the Antigravity CLI (agy) with the lessons MCP · 2. Install
chunks.text:
## 2. Install

The official command:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://antigravity.google/cli/install.sh | bash
```

- The path needs `/cli/`: `https://antigravity.google/install.sh`, which some docs show, answers 404.
- **Read the script before running it** (`curl -fsSL ... | less`). What it does:
  - no sudo
  - downloads the binary from an updater on Google Cloud Run and checks its SHA-512
  - puts it at `~/.local/bin/agy` and removes the macOS quarantine flag
  - `agy install` appends `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"` to both `~/.zshrc` and `~/.profile`
- During the install you will see lines like `ERROR: logging before google.Init: I1102 ...`. They are INFO logs (the leading `I`), not real errors; the script ends with exit 0.
- At the end: `✅ Antigravity CLI installed successfully at ~/.local/bin/agy`. Open a new terminal or `source ~/.zshrc`, then try `agy --version`.

chunks.title: 3. First sign-in
chunks.label: Use the Antigravity CLI (agy) with the lessons MCP · 3. First sign-in
chunks.text:
## 3. First sign-in

Run `agy` (or your first `agy -p`) and it prints a Google sign-in URL.

1. Open it with **"→ Click here to authenticate"** (do not copy it by hand; see step 4).
2. Sign in to Google; antigravity.google shows a code starting with `4/0...`.
3. Paste the code into agy's prompt and press Enter (`agy -p` waits only 60 seconds for it; if that is too short, sign in with plain `agy` first).
4. The next screen asks about data sharing; see step 5.
5. "Do you trust the contents of this project?": answer **Yes, I trust this folder** only for a folder you really trust.

Then the banner shows the version, the account's plan and the model.

chunks.title: 4. Trap: a cut URL makes Google answer invalid_scope
chunks.label: Use the Antigravity CLI (agy) with the lessons MCP · 4. Trap: a cut URL makes Google answer invalid_scope
chunks.text:
## 4. Trap: a cut URL makes Google answer invalid_scope

The sign-in URL is very long. agy shows it in a box with a pager (`(1–16 of 29 lines)`, scroll with shift+↑/↓). Copying only the visible part with the mouse cuts the URL mid-word.

What happened for real: the URL was cut inside the word `experimentsandconfigs`, and Google answered

```
Access blocked: Authorization Error
Error 400: invalid_scope (invalid=.../auth/experiments)
```

- **Fix**: press "→ Click here to authenticate", or scroll the box to the end; a complete URL ends with `&state=...`.
- General lesson: an error saying the scope is wrong is often not a permission problem but an incomplete URL.

chunks.title: 5. Trap: the pre-ticked data-sharing box
chunks.label: Use the Antigravity CLI (agy) with the lessons MCP · 5. Trap: the pre-ticked data-sharing box
chunks.text:
## 5. Trap: the pre-ticked data-sharing box

After the code, this box appears **already ticked**:

```
[x] Yes, I agree to help improve Antigravity CLI by allowing Google to collect and use my Interactions data
```

- Pressing Done straight away means Google may collect and use your conversations.
- Nat chose to untick it: press Enter on the box to toggle it, then Done.
- What this workshop suggests: read every box before Done, especially the ones ticked for you, and decide yourself whether to share.

chunks.title: 6. The agy mcp commands
chunks.label: Use the Antigravity CLI (agy) with the lessons MCP · 6. The agy mcp commands
chunks.text:
## 6. The agy mcp commands

```
$ agy mcp --help
Usage: agy mcp <subcommand> [flags] [args]

Available subcommands:
  add      Add or update an MCP server configuration
  remove   Remove an MCP server configuration
  list     List all configured MCP servers
  enable   Enable an MCP server
  disable  Disable an MCP server

Run "agy mcp <subcommand> --help" for flags, argument rules, and examples.
(exit 0)
```

The flags of `add`:

```
$ agy mcp add --help
Usage: agy mcp add [flags] <name> <commandOrUrl> [args...]

Add or update an MCP server configuration

Flags:
  -H        Short alias for --header (default [])
  -e        Short alias for --env (default [])
  --env     Environment variable KEY=value (repeatable) (default [])
  -h        Show help
  --header  HTTP header Key: Value (repeatable) (default [])
  --help    Show help
  -t        Short alias for --type (default stdio)
  --type    Server type: 'stdio' or 'http' (default stdio)

Arguments:
  <name>          Unique name for the server.
  <commandOrUrl>  Executable for a stdio server, or the URL for an http server.
  [args...]       Arguments passed to the stdio command.

Notes:
  Flags must come before <name>; a flag placed after it is rejected.
  http/https URLs are detected automatically, so --type is usually unnecessary.
  Use -- before the command to pass a command or args that begin with '-'.

Examples:
  agy mcp add fs npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem /work
  agy mcp add --header "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN" api https://example.com/mcp
  agy mcp add --env GITHUB_TOKEN=xxx gh -- docker run -i ghcr.io/github/mcp
(exit 0)
```

The two most important lines in Notes:

- **Flags must come before `<name>`**; a flag after the name is rejected, with an error that never mentions flags (section 8).
- URLs starting with http/https are detected as `http` automatically; no `--type` needed.

chunks.title: 7. Add the lessons MCP
chunks.label: Use the Antigravity CLI (agy) with the lessons MCP · 7. Add the lessons MCP
chunks.text:
## 7. Add the lessons MCP

Two servers, the same tools (`search`, `fetch`, `get_image`, `list_lessons`):

- `aiexpo`: the server on Cloudflare; searches by meaning and by words
- `aiexpo-github`: fetched from GitHub by `npx` and run on your machine; searches by words, works even if Cloudflare is down

```
$ agy mcp add aiexpo https://aiexpo.buildwithoracle.com/mcp; agy mcp add aiexpo-github npx -y github:Caeruleus-Lab/aiexpo-lessons-mcp
Added MCP server "aiexpo" (http)
Added MCP server "aiexpo-github" (stdio)
(exit 0)
```

`add` is "add or update": running it again changes nothing and creates no duplicate.

```
$ agy mcp list
NAME           TYPE   STATUS   COMMAND/URL
aiexpo         http   enabled  https://aiexpo.buildwithoracle.com/mcp
aiexpo-github  stdio  enabled  npx -y github:Caeruleus-Lab/aiexpo-lessons-mcp
(exit 0)
```

Other MCP servers already on your machine show up in this list too (left out of the capture).

chunks.title: 8. Trap: a flag after the name
chunks.label: Use the Antigravity CLI (agy) with the lessons MCP · 8. Trap: a flag after the name
chunks.text:
## 8. Trap: a flag after the name

```
$ agy mcp add try-x https://example.com/mcp --header 'X-Test: 1'   # flag after the name
Error: http server type does not accept command arguments
(exit 1)
```

The error does not say the flag is misplaced. Everything after `<commandOrUrl>` counts as arguments for the command, and an http server has no command to pass them to, so agy answers `http server type does not accept command arguments`. When you see this error, check the flag order first.

The right order: `agy mcp add --header "X-Test: 1" try-x https://example.com/mcp` (the capture script removes `try-x` if it was added).

chunks.title: 9. Disable for a while, then enable again
chunks.label: Use the Antigravity CLI (agy) with the lessons MCP · 9. Disable for a while, then enable again
chunks.text:
## 9. Disable for a while, then enable again

No need to remove a server; disable it:

```
$ agy mcp disable aiexpo-github; agy mcp list; agy mcp enable aiexpo-github
Disabled MCP server "aiexpo-github"
NAME           TYPE   STATUS    COMMAND/URL
aiexpo         http   enabled   https://aiexpo.buildwithoracle.com/mcp
aiexpo-github  stdio  disabled  npx -y github:Caeruleus-Lab/aiexpo-lessons-mcp
Enabled MCP server "aiexpo-github"
aiexpo-github  stdio  enabled  npx -y github:Caeruleus-Lab/aiexpo-lessons-mcp
(exit 0)
```

chunks.title: 10. Test with agy -p
chunks.label: Use the Antigravity CLI (agy) with the lessons MCP · 10. Test with agy -p
chunks.text:
## 10. Test with agy -p

`-p` asks once and exits, good for scripts and tests. The flags used:

- `--sandbox`: the agent works inside a sandbox
- `--dangerously-skip-permissions`: no prompt before each tool call. In `-p` nobody is there to press Allow, so it is needed; use it only together with `--sandbox` and with read-only MCP servers like these.
- `--print-timeout 240s`: wait at most 4 minutes for the answer

Ask through the Cloudflare server:

```
$ agy --sandbox --dangerously-skip-permissions --print-timeout 240s -p "Use ONLY the MCP server aiexpo ... how do I build my own MCP server?"
- **Implement the JSON-RPC 2.0 handlers**: Create a script (starting from the 59-line dependency-free `mini-mcp.mjs`) that handles `initialize`, `tools/list` (declaring your tool names and JSON Schemas in `TOOLS`), and `tools/call` (running your tool logic and returning `{ content: [{ type: "text", text }] }`), while ignoring notifications without an `id`.
- **Add your data and choose a transport**: Swap `NOTES` for your own data (or pre-chunked/embedded data like `chunks.json`), and expose the handler either via **stdio** (reading one JSON line per `stdin` and writing responses strictly to `stdout`) or **Streamable HTTP** (accepting `POST` requests at `/mcp`, e.g., on a Cloudflare Worker).
- **Test and register with your client**: Verify responses using `stdio` pipes or `curl`, then connect the server to your AI client (e.g., `claude mcp add mini -- node /path/to/mini-mcp.mjs` for local stdio, or adding the `/mcp` URL as a custom connector in claude.ai and ChatGPT).

**Lesson URL:** https://aiexpo.buildwithoracle.com/2026-11-02_build-mcp-lesson/en

**MCP tools called:**
- `aiexpo` → `search`
- `aiexpo` → `fetch`
(exit 0)
```

Ask through the GitHub server:

```
$ agy --sandbox --dangerously-skip-permissions --print-timeout 240s -p "Use ONLY the MCP server aiexpo-github ... list_lessons, then search"
- **Lesson count**: 7
- **Title of lesson 7**:
  - **English**: Build your own MCP: turn lessons into tools for AI
  - **Thai**: สร้าง MCP ของตัวเอง: จากบทเรียนเป็นเครื่องมือให้ AI
- **Top hit ID**: `build-mcp/en/3`
- **MCP tool names called** (on server `aiexpo-github`): `list_lessons`, `search`
(exit 0)
```

Both answer from the real lessons and name the tools they called. If agy answers without calling any tool, check that `agy mcp list` shows `STATUS` `enabled`.

chunks.title: 11. All the traps in one place
chunks.label: Use the Antigravity CLI (agy) with the lessons MCP · 11. All the traps in one place
chunks.text:
## 11. All the traps in one place

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `install.sh` answers 404 | URL without `/cli/` | `https://antigravity.google/cli/install.sh` |
| `ERROR: logging before google.Init` during install | INFO-level log | Nothing to do; check the exit code |
| No `agy` command although the Antigravity app is installed | The desktop app does not include the CLI | Install the CLI separately |
| `Error 400: invalid_scope` | Sign-in URL copied incompletely | Press "Click here to authenticate", or scroll until you see `&state=` |
| Sharing data without noticing | The box comes pre-ticked | Press Enter to untick it before Done |
| `agy -p` sign-in times out | It waits only 60 seconds for the code | Sign in with plain `agy` first |
| `http server type does not accept command arguments` | Flag placed after the name, read as arguments | Put every flag before `<name>` |

## 1. Antigravity CLI คืออะไร

Antigravity CLI คือ coding agent ของ Google ที่รันใน terminal คำสั่งชื่อ `agy` ใช้โมเดล Gemini ตามบัญชีที่ล็อกอิน (เครื่องนี้เป็น Google AI Pro โมเดล "Gemini 4 Argon (Medium)")

- **แอป Antigravity บนเดสก์ท็อป (2.3.1) ไม่มีคำสั่ง `agy` มาให้** ต้องติดตั้ง CLI แยก
- `agy` ต่อ MCP ได้ทั้งสองแบบ: `http` (URL) กับ `stdio` (คำสั่งที่รันในเครื่อง)

```
$ agy --version
1.4.12
(exit 0)
```

![สรุปบนหน้าจอ: เพิ่ม MCP สองตัวใน agy, agy mcp list ขึ้น enabled ทั้งคู่, agy -p ตอบจาก aiexpo-github ว่ามี 7 บทเรียน และกับดักสามอันตอนล็อกอินและตอนเพิ่ม](images/01-agy-mcp.png)

chunks.title: 2. ติดตั้ง
chunks.label: ใช้ Antigravity CLI (agy) กับ MCP ของบทเรียน · 2. ติดตั้ง
chunks.text:
## 2. ติดตั้ง

คำสั่งทางการ:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://antigravity.google/cli/install.sh | bash
```

- ต้องมี `/cli/` ในพาธ `https://antigravity.google/install.sh` ที่บางเอกสารเขียนไว้ตอบ 404
- **อ่านสคริปต์ก่อนรัน** (`curl -fsSL ... | less`) สิ่งที่มันทำ:
  - ไม่ใช้ sudo
  - ดาวน์โหลดตัวโปรแกรมจาก updater บน Google Cloud Run แล้วตรวจ SHA-512
  - วางไว้ที่ `~/.local/bin/agy` แล้วลบ flag quarantine ของ macOS
  - `agy install` เติม `export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"` ลงทั้ง `~/.zshrc` และ `~/.profile`
- ระหว่างติดตั้งจะเห็นบรรทัด `ERROR: logging before google.Init: I1102 ...` นี่เป็น log ระดับ INFO (ตัว `I` นำหน้า) ไม่ใช่ error จริง สคริปต์จบด้วย exit 0
- จบแล้วจะขึ้น `✅ Antigravity CLI installed successfully at ~/.local/bin/agy` เปิด terminal ใหม่ หรือ `source ~/.zshrc` แล้วลอง `agy --version`

chunks.title: 3. ล็อกอินครั้งแรก
chunks.label: ใช้ Antigravity CLI (agy) กับ MCP ของบทเรียน · 3. ล็อกอินครั้งแรก
chunks.text:
## 3. ล็อกอินครั้งแรก

พิมพ์ `agy` (หรือ `agy -p` ครั้งแรก) จะขึ้น URL สำหรับล็อกอิน Google

1. เปิด URL ด้วย **"→ Click here to authenticate"** (อย่า copy เอง ดูข้อ 4)
2. ล็อกอินบัญชี Google หน้า antigravity.google จะโชว์รหัสขึ้นต้นด้วย `4/0...`
3. วางรหัสใน prompt ของ agy กด Enter (`agy -p` รอรหัสแค่ 60 วินาที ถ้าช้าให้ล็อกอินผ่าน `agy` ธรรมดาก่อน)
4. หน้าถัดไปถามเรื่องแชร์ข้อมูล ดูข้อ 5
5. "Do you trust the contents of this project?" ตอบ **Yes, I trust this folder** เฉพาะโฟลเดอร์ที่เราไว้ใจจริง

เสร็จแล้ว banner จะบอกเวอร์ชัน แผนของบัญชี และโมเดล

chunks.title: 4. กับดัก: URL ขาด จน Google ตอบ invalid_scope
chunks.label: ใช้ Antigravity CLI (agy) กับ MCP ของบทเรียน · 4. กับดัก: URL ขาด จน Google ตอบ invalid_scope
chunks.text:
## 4. กับดัก: URL ขาด จน Google ตอบ invalid_scope

URL ล็อกอินยาวมาก agy วางไว้ในกล่องที่มี pager (`(1–16 of 29 lines)` เลื่อนด้วย shift+↑/↓) ถ้าลากเมาส์ copy แค่ส่วนที่เห็น URL จะขาดกลางคำ

ที่เจอจริง: URL ขาดตรงกลางคำ `experimentsandconfigs` Google ตอบหน้า

```
Access blocked: Authorization Error
Error 400: invalid_scope (invalid=.../auth/experiments)
```

- **ทางแก้**: กด "→ Click here to authenticate" หรือเลื่อนกล่องจนสุด URL ที่ครบจะจบด้วย `&state=...`
- บทเรียนทั่วไป: error ที่บอกว่า scope ผิด มักไม่ใช่ปัญหาสิทธิ์ แต่เป็น URL ที่ไม่ครบ

chunks.title: 5. กับดัก: กล่องแชร์ข้อมูลที่ติ๊กไว้ให้แล้ว
chunks.label: ใช้ Antigravity CLI (agy) กับ MCP ของบทเรียน · 5. กับดัก: กล่องแชร์ข้อมูลที่ติ๊กไว้ให้แล้ว
chunks.text:
## 5. กับดัก: กล่องแชร์ข้อมูลที่ติ๊กไว้ให้แล้ว

หลังวางรหัส จะเจอกล่องนี้ **ติ๊กไว้ให้แล้ว**:

```
[x] Yes, I agree to help improve Antigravity CLI by allowing Google to collect and use my Interactions data
```

- ถ้ากด Done เลย แปลว่ายอมให้ Google เก็บบทสนทนาไปใช้
- Nat เลือกเอาติ๊กออก: กด Enter ที่กล่องเพื่อสลับ แล้วค่อย Done
- เวิร์กช็อปนี้แนะนำ: อ่านทุกกล่องก่อนกด Done โดยเฉพาะกล่องที่ติ๊กมาให้แล้ว เลือกเองว่าจะแชร์หรือไม่

chunks.label: ใช้ Antigravity CLI (agy) กับ MCP ของบทเรียน · 6. คำสั่ง agy mcp

## 6. คำสั่ง agy mcp

```
$ agy mcp --help
Usage: agy mcp <subcommand> [flags] [args]

Available subcommands:
  add      Add or update an MCP server configuration
  remove   Remove an MCP server configuration
  list     List all configured MCP servers
  enable   Enable an MCP server
  disable  Disable an MCP server

Run "agy mcp <subcommand> --help" for flags, argument rules, and examples.
(exit 0)
```

ตัวเลือกของ `add`:

```
$ agy mcp add --help
Usage: agy mcp add [flags] <name> <commandOrUrl> [args...]

Add or update an MCP server configuration

Flags:
  -H        Short alias for --header (default [])
  -e        Short alias for --env (default [])
  --env     Environment variable KEY=value (repeatable) (default [])
  -h        Show help
  --header  HTTP header Key: Value (repeatable) (default [])
  --help    Show help
  -t        Short alias for --type (default stdio)
  --type    Server type: 'stdio' or 'http' (default stdio)

Arguments:
  <name>          Unique name for the server.
  <commandOrUrl>  Executable for a stdio server, or the URL for an http server.
  [args...]       Arguments passed to the stdio command.

Notes:
  Flags must come before <name>; a flag placed after it is rejected.
  http/https URLs are detected automatically, so --type is usually unnecessary.
  Use -- before the command to pass a command or args that begin with '-'.

Examples:
  agy mcp add fs npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem /work
  agy mcp add --header "Authorization: Bearer TOKEN" api https://example.com/mcp
  agy mcp add --env GITHUB_TOKEN=xxx gh -- docker run -i ghcr.io/github/mcp
(exit 0)
```

สองบรรทัดที่สำคัญที่สุดใน Notes:

- **flag ต้องมาก่อน `<name>`** วางหลังชื่อจะโดนปฏิเสธ ด้วย error ที่ไม่ได้พูดถึง flag เลย (ข้อ 8)
- URL ที่ขึ้นต้นด้วย http/https ถูกจับเป็น `http` อัตโนมัติ ไม่ต้องใส่ `--type`

- **Test and register with your client**: Verify responses using `stdio` pipes or `curl`, then connect the server to your AI client (e.g., `claude mcp add mini -- node /path/to/mini-mcp.mjs` for local stdio, or adding the `/mcp` URL as a custom connector in claude.ai and ChatGPT).

## 11. กับดักทั้งหมดในที่เดียว

| อาการ | สาเหตุ | ทางแก้ |

| `install.sh` ตอบ 404 | ใช้ URL ที่ไม่มี `/cli/` | `https://antigravity.google/cli/install.sh` |

| ยอมแชร์ข้อมูลโดยไม่รู้ตัว | กล่องติ๊กมาให้แล้ว | Enter เพื่อเอาติ๊กออก ก่อน Done |

chunks.text:
## 3. The full skill, as a .md file

`list_skills` says which skills exist; `get_skill` sends the whole skill.

```
awaken      ปลุก Oracle: ถาม 3 ข้อ แล้วสร้าง CLAUDE.md + ψ/memory/resonance
rrr         รายงานจบงาน: Timeline เวลาจริง + บทเรียน
forward     ส่งต่องาน: เขียน handoff ให้แชทถัดไป (ทำอะไรไป ค้างอะไร เริ่มตรงไหน)
recap       เริ่มงาน (Claude Code เท่านั้น ในแชทใช้ไม่ได้): อ่าน handoff และรายงานรอบก่อน บอกว่าค้างอะไร
workshop    workshop สั้นในแชทเดียว: awaken → งานจริง → คุย → /rrr พร้อม time log
awaken-app  สร้างแอปปลุก Oracle แบบกดได้ (artifact / canvas)
where-we-are เราอยู่ตรงไหน: สรุปแชทนี้ ทำอะไรไป ตอนนี้ทำอะไร อะไรยังค้าง (ใช้ในแชทได้ ไม่เหมือน /recap)
```

`get_skill {name: "rrr"}` answers in two parts: one line of text and one `text/markdown` file.

```
content parts: ['text', 'resource']
[resource] uri:      https://aiexpo.buildwithoracle.com/oracle/full/rrr.md
           mimeType: text/markdown
           size:     32,103 bytes
           files inside:
             - skills/rrr/SKILL.md
             - skills/rrr/HOSTS.md
             - skills/rrr/TEMPLATE.md
             - skills/rrr/scripts/session-clock.py
```

- **Part 1** says how to run it in a chat with no terminal
- **Part 2** is every file of the real skill folder from `Soul-Brews-Studio/arra-oracle-skills-cli` (branch `alpha`), not a summary
- The file ends with the ZIP link and install steps, so the AI can pass them on
- `source` options: `full` (default) · `chat` (part 1 only) · `github` (the live SKILL.md)

![claude.ai fetches the full rrr skill through the MCP: names all 4 files and what each does, then gives the ZIP link and install steps](images/03-claude-full-rrr.png)

chunks.text:
## 4. Tried for real in claude.ai: /awaken → work → /rrr → /forward

One chat, nothing installed. All times are real, 4 Nov 2026 (GMT+7).

**4.1 /awaken.** Typed: "ใช้ AIExpo lessons: มี skill อะไรบ้าง แล้วเปิด /awaken มาปลุก Oracle ให้ฉันเลย" (use AIExpo lessons: which skills are there, then open /awaken and wake an Oracle for me)

- The AI called `list_skills`, then `get_skill awaken`, and opened the full skill
- It followed the real skill's steps: system check, language, Fast or Soul Sync, 5 questions, a theme
- Result: "โคมเล็ก Oracle" (Little Lamp Oracle) with `CLAUDE.md`, the `ψ/` files and a first commit, downloadable as tar.gz
- 19:57 → 20:00

![Little Lamp Oracle born in claude.ai: a table of Oracle, Human, Born 4 Nov 2026, Mode Fast, Duration 2 minutes, and the files created](images/04-proof-awaken.png)

**4.2 One real task.** Asked for a 65-minute workshop outline; the AI read `list_lessons` and drafted 5 parts with the risks.

**4.3 /rrr.** Typed: "พอแค่นี้ก่อน ทำ /rrr ให้หน่อย" (that's it for now, do /rrr)

- A retrospective, a lesson and a metrics row, as `.md` files
- Timeline 19:56–20:01, every row from the real message times
- The AI looked for the session clock as the skill says, found none, and wrote `evidence: none` instead of guessing (that step is only in the full skill's `HOSTS.md`)

![The /rrr report in claude.ai: Session Retrospective with a Timeline from 19:56 to 20:01 and the files changed](images/05-proof-rrr.png)

**4.4 /forward.** Typed: "ขอบคุณ แล้วทำ /forward ส่งต่อให้แชทพรุ่งนี้ด้วย" (thanks, now /forward to tomorrow's chat)

- A file `ψ/inbox/handoff/2026-11-04_20-02_….md`: what we did, what is open, where to start next time
- The real skill then enters plan mode, so claude.ai asked to Approve a plan; we pressed Keep planning

![The /forward handoff in claude.ai: the plan box waiting for Approve and the handoff file open on the right](images/06-proof-forward.png)

> Typing `/rrr` at the start of a line in claude.ai opens its own slash menu, which eats the command. Put it mid-sentence: "ทำ /rrr ให้หน่อย".

chunks.title: 5. /recap runs only in Claude Code
chunks.label: One MCP hands out skills, voice and video · 5. /recap runs only in Claude Code
chunks.text:
## 5. /recap runs only in Claude Code

`/recap` reads the `ψ/` files on disk, the git log and the session history. A chat has none of these, so there is no chat `/recap`; `get_skill recap` says so plainly and tells the person what to do instead:

```
# /recap: Claude Code only

> For the AI reading this page. `/recap` does not run in a chat (claude.ai, ChatGPT, Gemini).
  It needs Claude Code (the CLI) in the Oracle's folder ... Do not pretend to run it.
```

- In Claude Code: open a terminal in the Oracle's folder, run `claude`, type `/recap`
- In a chat: attach the `/forward` handoff and ask to continue from "Next Session"

Full output: [captures/04-recap-cli-only.txt](captures/04-recap-cli-only.txt)

### /where-we-are works in a chat (added 5 Nov 2026)

`/where-we-are` is `/recap --now deep`: a mid-session "where are we". Unlike `/recap`, it reads **this conversation**, not files on disk, so it runs in a chat. `get_skill where-we-are` hands over the whole thing, 6 files (the where-we-are skill and the recap skill it calls):

```
[resource] uri:      https://aiexpo.buildwithoracle.com/oracle/full/where-we-are.md
           files inside:
             - skills/where-we-are/SKILL.md
             - skills/recap/SKILL.md
             - skills/recap/references/rich-paths.md
             - skills/recap/recap-rich.ts
             - skills/recap/recap.ts
             - skills/recap/skills-staleness.ts
```

- The AI answers in four parts: a table of this session (topics, tagged spark / complete / park / return / escape), status (now · done · open · parked), the bigger picture, and its own read, then asks what next
- It must not invent times, files or results: only what is in the chat
- In claude.ai, if you connected the MCP before 5 Nov, disconnect and connect again (trap 2) to see this skill

Full output: [captures/09-get-skill-where-we-are.txt](captures/09-get-skill-where-we-are.txt)

chunks.text:
## 4. ลองจริงใน claude.ai: /awaken → งาน → /rrr → /forward

แชทเดียว ไม่ได้ติดตั้งอะไรเพิ่ม เวลาทั้งหมดเป็นเวลาจริงของวันที่ 4 พ.ย. 2026 (GMT+7)

**4.1 /awaken** พิมพ์ "ใช้ AIExpo lessons: มี skill อะไรบ้าง แล้วเปิด /awaken มาปลุก Oracle ให้ฉันเลย"

- AI เรียก `list_skills` แล้ว `get_skill awaken` เปิด skill ฉบับเต็ม
- ทำตามขั้นของ skill จริง: เช็กระบบ ถามภาษา ให้เลือก Fast หรือ Soul Sync ถาม 5 ข้อ เสนอ theme
- ได้ "โคมเล็ก Oracle" พร้อม `CLAUDE.md` ไฟล์ใน `ψ/` และ commit แรก ดาวน์โหลดเป็น tar.gz ได้
- ใช้เวลา 19:57 → 20:00

![โคมเล็ก Oracle เกิดใน claude.ai: ตาราง Oracle, Human, Born 4 พ.ย. 2026, Mode Fast, Duration 2 นาที และไฟล์ที่สร้าง](images/04-proof-awaken.png)

**4.2 งานจริงหนึ่งชิ้น** ขอโครงเวิร์กช็อป 65 นาที AI อ่าน `list_lessons` แล้วร่าง 5 ช่วงพร้อมจุดเสี่ยง

**4.3 /rrr** พิมพ์ "พอแค่นี้ก่อน ทำ /rrr ให้หน่อย"

- ได้ retrospective, บทเรียน และ metrics เป็นไฟล์ `.md`
- Timeline 19:56–20:01 ทุกบรรทัดมาจากเวลาจริงของข้อความ
- AI ลองหา session clock ตามที่ skill สั่ง ไม่เจอ แล้วเขียนตรง ๆ ว่า `evidence: none` ไม่เดาเวลา (ขั้นนี้อยู่ใน `HOSTS.md` ของ skill ฉบับเต็มเท่านั้น)

![รายงาน /rrr ใน claude.ai: Session Retrospective พร้อม Timeline 19:56 ถึง 20:01 และไฟล์ที่แก้](images/05-proof-rrr.png)

**4.4 /forward** พิมพ์ "ขอบคุณ แล้วทำ /forward ส่งต่อให้แชทพรุ่งนี้ด้วย"

- ได้ไฟล์ `ψ/inbox/handoff/2026-11-04_20-02_….md`: ทำอะไรไป ค้างอะไร รอบหน้าเริ่มตรงไหน
- skill ตัวจริงสั่งให้เข้า plan mode ต่อ claude.ai จึงถามว่าจะ Approve แผนไหม เรากด Keep planning ไม่ให้ทำต่อ

![handoff จาก /forward ใน claude.ai: กล่องแผนรอ Approve และไฟล์ handoff เปิดอยู่ด้านขวา](images/06-proof-forward.png)

> พิมพ์ `/rrr` ต้นบรรทัดใน claude.ai เมนู slash ของมันจะกินคำสั่ง พิมพ์กลางประโยคแทน เช่น "ทำ /rrr ให้หน่อย"

chunks.text:
## 5. /recap ใช้ได้เฉพาะ Claude Code

`/recap` อ่านไฟล์ `ψ/` ในเครื่อง git log และประวัติ session แชทไม่มีของพวกนี้ เราจึงไม่ทำ `/recap` ฉบับแชท `get_skill recap` ตอบตรง ๆ ว่าใช้ไม่ได้ และบอกคนว่าทำอะไรแทน:

```
# /recap: Claude Code only

> For the AI reading this page. `/recap` does not run in a chat (claude.ai, ChatGPT, Gemini).
  It needs Claude Code (the CLI) in the Oracle's folder ... Do not pretend to run it.
```

- ใน Claude Code: เปิดเทอร์มินัลในโฟลเดอร์ Oracle รัน `claude` แล้วพิมพ์ `/recap`
- ในแชท: แนบไฟล์ handoff จาก `/forward` แล้วบอกให้ทำต่อจาก "Next Session"

ผลเต็ม: [captures/04-recap-cli-only.txt](captures/04-recap-cli-only.txt)

### /where-we-are ใช้ในแชทได้ (เพิ่ม 5 พ.ย. 2026)

`/where-we-are` คือ `/recap --now deep` ถามกลางงานว่า "เราอยู่ตรงไหน" ต่างจาก `/recap` ตรงที่มันอ่านจาก**บทสนทนานี้เอง** ไม่ต้องมีไฟล์ในเครื่อง จึงใช้ในแชทได้ `get_skill where-we-are` ส่งมาทั้งก้อน 6 ไฟล์ (skill where-we-are กับ recap ที่มันเรียกใช้):

```
[resource] uri:      https://aiexpo.buildwithoracle.com/oracle/full/where-we-are.md
           files inside:
             - skills/where-we-are/SKILL.md
             - skills/recap/SKILL.md
             - skills/recap/references/rich-paths.md
             - skills/recap/recap-rich.ts
             - skills/recap/recap.ts
             - skills/recap/skills-staleness.ts
```

- AI ตอบเป็น 4 ส่วน: ตาราง session นี้ (หัวข้อ และป้าย spark / complete / park / return / escape) · สถานะ (ตอนนี้ · เสร็จ · ค้าง · พักไว้) · ภาพใหญ่ · ความเห็นของ AI แล้วถามว่าไปต่อตรงไหน
- ห้ามแต่งเวลา ไฟล์ หรือผลลัพธ์ ใช้เฉพาะสิ่งที่อยู่ในแชท
- ใน claude.ai ถ้าต่อ MCP ไว้ก่อนวันที่ 5 พ.ย. ให้ตัดแล้วต่อใหม่ (กับดักข้อ 2) จึงจะเห็น skill นี้

ผลเต็ม: [captures/09-get-skill-where-we-are.txt](captures/09-get-skill-where-we-are.txt)
