chunks.text:
## 5. The real demo: `/herdr-promote neo back session` (22:14-22:19)

![Nat types /herdr-promote neo back session while Neo is still in the laris-co sidebar](images/03-promote-neo-back.png)

- Nat saw Neo had too much going on to live in the shared session, so Neo should get its own (in the recording: Neo gets a place of its own, in its own session; when we want to work with Neo, we go there).
- At 22:13 Nat had typed `/herdr-promote neo` once; the running call shows Interrupted and Nat asked about something else. The run that did the work is 22:14.
- The agent started with `--dry`: `herdr-promote neo --to neo --from laris-co --dry`.
- This time it moved one space at a time, worktrees first, Neo main last: `herdr-move --workspace <w> --from laris-co --to neo`.
- 7 agents made it back to `neo`. Neo main (`wFK`) hit the same block again; the agent resumed `08f33511` and the builder `840b12d9` by hand.
- It put the pane names back, restored the `~/.local/bin/neo` link, and closed the empty spaces in laris-co with `workspace close wFK --group`.

![Sidebar before and after: at 22:13 neo-oracle, relic5 and people-oracle are in laris-co; at 22:19 they are gone, line-profile-picture-webhook is left](images/04-sidebar-before-after.png)

- Result: session `neo` holds 9 agents: `w1:p1` Neo main, `w1:p2` builder-neo, `w2`-`w4` worktrees, `w5` people-oracle, `w6`-`w8` relic-extract, relic5, relic4-scan.
- One pane stayed in laris-co (`wFW`): a fresh Claude that was never used, stuck at "Yes, I trust this folder". The agent left that to Nat: "I won't answer that for you."

chunks.title: 6. Before a real move
chunks.label: herdr bring, move, promote: move agents between sessions without losing the conversation · 6. Before a real move
chunks.text:
## 6. Before a real move

- **`--dry` first, always:** it lists every member and marks the pane running it (`← this pane: it would be skipped`).
- **Run it from a pane outside the set:** the tool refuses to move its own pane. `!` in a member's pane counts as that pane.
- **Everyone idle:** a `working` agent loses its turn if moved.
- **Discord bots:** check `ps -o args= -p <pid>` for `--channels`. With it, the resumed body comes back without its bot: relaunch with the flags, or do not move it.
- **The repo needs an `origin` remote:** `maw herdr ticket open` requires it.
- **Test only on throwaway agents in scratch sessions**, never on live team bodies.

chunks.title: 7. After the move
chunks.label: herdr bring, move, promote: move agents between sessions without losing the conversation · 7. After the move
chunks.text:
## 7. After the move

1. **Names:** resumed panes come back without herdr names. `herdr --session <to> agent rename <pane> <name>` (unpromote does it for you).
2. **Room:** room state is saved per session, so the old room does not follow. Let the team's desk rebuild it from the charter (see [herdr-room](../2026-10-31_herdr-room-lesson/) and [team charters](../2026-11-05_team-ecosystem-lesson/)).
3. **Charter:** set `session:` in `laris-team/teams/<team>.yaml`.
4. **Open it:** `herdr --session <to>`, or make a link `ln -s herdr-by-name ~/.local/bin/<session>`.
5. **Check for duplicates:** `/herdr-info <oracle>` should say `warnings: none`.

chunks.title: 8. Real traps
chunks.label: herdr bring, move, promote: move agents between sessions without losing the conversation · 8. Real traps
chunks.text:
## 8. Real traps

- **A space with linked worktrees will not close:** `herdr-move` stopped halfway three times in one day (phonebooth, Neo out, Neo back). Neo main was ended but not resumed and had to be resumed by hand by id. The agent proposed closing with `--group`.
- **Two resumes into one pane:** resuming Neo main and the builder, both reported `w1:p1`. The second command sat unsent in Neo main's input box; the agent cleared it with one ctrl+c, then split a new pane for the builder.
- **A pane that was never used comes back as a new Claude:** there is no history to resume (`wFP`, `wFW`).
- **The model resets:** an agent started with `--model haiku` comes back on the default model.
- **`/exit` stops at a dialog:** feedback drafts or background tasks ask first. Never answer for the human, and never pick "Move to background": the old process keeps running and you get two writers.
- **The agent name is cleared on resume:** the space label survives, the agent name goes to None. Rename again and address panes by id.
- **Pane ids repeat across sessions:** `w8:p2` existed in two. Always pass `--session`.
- **Unpromote right after a promote:** an agent resumed but not yet detected makes the source look empty, so unpromote moves nothing. Wait a few seconds.

chunks.title: 2. ห้าคำสั่ง ต่างกันตรงไหน
chunks.label: herdr bring, move, promote: ย้าย agent ข้าม session บทสนทนาไม่หาย · 2. ห้าคำสั่ง ต่างกันตรงไหน
chunks.text:
## 2. ห้าคำสั่ง ต่างกันตรงไหน

- **`/herdr-bring <handle>`**: เอา maw handle (oracle ที่ maw รู้จัก) เข้ามามี space ของตัวเองใน herdr ถ้ามีประวัติ Claude ของ repo นั้นจะ resume ต่อ ถ้ามี tmux session ของ maw ที่ยังรันอยู่และว่าง จะปิดมันก่อน ถ้าไม่มีอะไรเลยจะเริ่มใหม่
- **`/herdr-bring-beside <who>`**: ดึง pane หนึ่งมาไว้ข้างฉันในแท็บเดียวกัน (ขวาหรือล่าง) ใช้ `herdr pane move` ตรง ๆ agent ไม่ได้ปิด ได้แค่ใน session เดียวกัน
- **`/herdr-move <oracle>`**: ย้าย oracle หนึ่งตัว (ทุก agent ของ repo นั้น ทั้ง main และ worktree) ไป session ของตัวเอง ชื่อตั้งต้นคือชื่อ repo ตัด `-oracle` ออก เป็นเครื่องมือที่คำสั่งอื่นเรียกใช้
- **`/herdr-promote <team|repo|wXX>`**: ให้ทีม repo หรือ space หนึ่ง มี session ของตัวเอง ทีม (`<x>-team`) พา desk และทุก `wt/<oracle>` ไปด้วย ข้างในเรียก `herdr-move`
- **`/herdr-unpromote <team|oracle|session>`**: พากลับ ค่าตั้งต้นคือกลับมา session ของคนเรียก ตั้งชื่อ pane ให้ แล้วลบ session ต้นทางที่ว่างแล้ว
- ไม่ใช่การย้าย แต่ชื่อคล้ายกัน: **`/herdr-incubate <oracle>`** ตัด worktree ของ repo **ฉัน** เพื่อทำงานให้ oracle อื่น ไม่ได้เปิด repo ของมัน

> bring = เอาเข้ามา · bring-beside = มาข้างฉัน · move = oracle เดียวไปบ้านตัวเอง · promote = ทีมไปบ้านตัวเอง · unpromote = กลับบ้านเดิม

chunks.label: herdr bring, move, promote: ย้าย agent ข้าม session บทสนทนาไม่หาย · 3. เคล็ดลับเดียว: จบที่เดิม แล้ว resume ด้วย id เดิม
chunks.text:
## 3. เคล็ดลับเดียว: จบที่เดิม แล้ว resume ด้วย id เดิม

`herdr-move` ทำตามลำดับนี้ทุกครั้ง (จาก SKILL.md):

1. จบทุก agent ในชุดที่จะย้าย
2. รอจน id ทุกตัวหายไป (10 วินาที)
3. ปิด space ที่เหลือแต่ shell ว่าง ๆ worktree ก่อน
4. เปิด session ปลายทางถ้ายังไม่มี
5. resume ทีละตัว: `maw herdr ticket open <repo> --session <to> --session-id <id>`

- **ปิดก่อน แล้วค่อยเปิด ห้ามกลับลำดับ:** ถ้า resume ตอนตัวเก่ายังรัน จะมีสองตัวเขียน transcript เดียวกัน ข้อความปนกัน (herdr-bring บันทึกว่าเคยเกิดจริง)
- space ที่ยังมีอะไรรันอยู่ (เช่น server) ไม่ถูกปิด
- ถ้ามีตัวไหน resume ไม่ขึ้น คำสั่งจบด้วย exit 1 และพิมพ์บรรทัด `maw herdr ticket open …` ให้รันเอง

## 4. เดโมจริง: `/herdr-bring bring neo` (22:10)

![คำถามจาก agent ตอน bring neo: Neo อยู่ 3 ที่ ให้เลือกว่าจะรวม session neo เข้ามา, ย้าย bot body, หรือเปิดแค่ main](images/01-bring-neo-question.png)

- Nat อยู่ใน agent ประจำ session `laris-co` บนเครื่อง m5 พิมพ์ `/herdr-bring bring neo`
- `maw locate neo` ไม่คืน repo path และ Neo มีหลายร่างอยู่แล้ว agent จึงไม่เดา: "`/herdr-bring` can't settle this one by itself."
- มันถามว่า Neo อยู่ 3 ที่: bot body บน white, และ session `neo` บน m5 ให้เลือกสามทาง

chunks.title: 6. ก่อนย้ายจริง
chunks.label: herdr bring, move, promote: ย้าย agent ข้าม session บทสนทนาไม่หาย · 6. ก่อนย้ายจริง
chunks.text:
## 6. ก่อนย้ายจริง

- **`--dry` ก่อนเสมอ:** แสดงทุกตัวที่จะย้าย และ mark pane ที่รันคำสั่งไว้ (`← this pane: it would be skipped`)
- **รันจาก pane นอกชุดที่ย้าย:** คำสั่งไม่ยอมย้าย pane ของตัวเอง `!` ใน pane ของสมาชิกก็นับเป็น pane นั้น
- **ทุกตัวต้องว่าง:** ตัวที่กำลัง `working` ถ้าย้าย turn นั้นตาย
- **bot Discord:** เช็ก `ps -o args= -p <pid>` ว่ามี `--channels` ไหม ถ้ามี resume แล้ว bot หาย ต้องเปิดใหม่พร้อม flag หรืออย่าย้าย
- **repo ต้องมี `origin`:** `maw herdr ticket open` ต้องใช้
- **ทดสอบบน agent ทิ้งได้ใน session ทดลองเท่านั้น** ไม่ใช่บนร่างของทีมที่ใช้งานจริง

chunks.title: 7. หลังย้าย
chunks.label: herdr bring, move, promote: ย้าย agent ข้าม session บทสนทนาไม่หาย · 7. หลังย้าย
chunks.text:
## 7. หลังย้าย

1. **ชื่อ:** pane ที่ resume มาไม่มีชื่อ herdr ตั้งใหม่ `herdr --session <to> agent rename <pane> <name>` (unpromote ทำให้เอง)
2. **room:** room เก็บแยกตาม session room เก่าไม่ตามมา ให้ desk ของทีมสร้างใหม่ตาม charter (ดู [herdr-room](../2026-10-31_herdr-room-lesson/) และ [team charter](../2026-11-05_team-ecosystem-lesson/))
3. **charter:** ตั้ง `session:` ใน `laris-team/teams/<team>.yaml`
4. **เปิดดู:** `herdr --session <to>` หรือทำลิงก์ `ln -s herdr-by-name ~/.local/bin/<session>`
5. **ตรวจว่าไม่มีร่างซ้ำ:** `/herdr-info <oracle>` ต้องขึ้น `warnings: none`

chunks.title: 8. กับดักที่เจอจริง
chunks.label: herdr bring, move, promote: ย้าย agent ข้าม session บทสนทนาไม่หาย · 8. กับดักที่เจอจริง
chunks.text:
## 8. กับดักที่เจอจริง

- **space ที่มี worktree ผูกอยู่ปิดไม่ได้:** `herdr-move` ค้างครึ่งทางสามครั้งในวันเดียว (phonebooth, Neo ขาไป, Neo ขากลับ) Neo main ถูกจบแล้วแต่ไม่ถูก resume ต้อง resume เองด้วย id agent เสนอให้แก้เป็นปิดด้วย `--group`
- **resume สองตัวลง pane เดียว:** ตอน resume Neo main กับ builder ทั้งคู่รายงาน `w1:p1` คำสั่งที่สองไปค้างในกล่องพิมพ์ของ Neo main ยังไม่ถูกส่ง agent ล้างด้วย ctrl+c หนึ่งครั้ง แล้ว split pane ใหม่ให้ builder
- **pane ที่ไม่เคยถูกใช้กลับมาเป็น Claude ใหม่:** ไม่มีประวัติให้ resume (`wFP`, `wFW`)
- **model กลับเป็นค่าตั้งต้น:** agent ที่เปิดด้วย `--model haiku` กลับมาเป็น model ปกติ
- **`/exit` ค้างที่ dialog:** มี feedback draft หรือ background task จะถามก่อน ห้ามกดแทนคน ห้ามเลือก "Move to background" เพราะตัวเก่ายังรัน จะมีสองตัวเขียนซ้อน
- **ชื่อ agent หายหลัง resume:** label ของ space อยู่ แต่ชื่อ agent กลับเป็น None ต้องตั้งซ้ำ และอ้าง pane ด้วย id
- **pane id ซ้ำข้าม session:** `w8:p2` มีในสอง session ใส่ `--session` ทุกครั้ง
- **unpromote ทันทีหลัง promote:** agent ที่เพิ่ง resume ยังไม่ถูกตรวจเจอ ทำให้ต้นทางดูว่าง unpromote จะไม่ย้ายอะไร รอสักครู่

chunks.text:
## 1. The big picture

![Diagram of m5 and white over tailscale: m5 saves white as a machine, white answers back with herdr --machine m5-laris-co](images/00-m5-white-tailscale.png)

- **m5** is the Mac Nat works on. **white** is the Linux box (Ubuntu x86_64) that takes the heavy work.
- Both are on the same tailnet and reach each other by MagicDNS name, e.g. `white.follow-rankine.ts.net`.
- herdr on m5 saves white as a **machine** (one machine = one session on that box).
- ssh still runs underneath, but nobody types it ("ssh runs underneath; nobody types it", from `/herdr-link-talk`).

## 2. Local on top, machines below

- This frame is from part 2 at 27:15. Nat explains: the top is Local, your own machine; the bottom is called Machine, or Remote.
- Click `▸` beside a machine to unfold its spaces; it does not switch you away.
- A green dot beside the name = connected.
- Keyboard: `prefix+w`, then Up/Down, Enter (from `/herdr-machine-labels`).
- In part 1 at 07:00-07:45 Nat ran `uname -a` on each machine to show this one is a Mac and that one is Linux, then folded and unfolded each machine ("this is move number one"). Only the audio survives: the screen capture shows an empty draw.io tab, so there is no frame.

chunks.title: 3. Add a machine
chunks.label: herdr on many machines: add a machine, move a team to white, talk across · 3. Add a machine
chunks.text:
## 3. Add a machine

The real command from `/herdr-link-talk`:

```bash
# on m5: save white's laris-co session as a machine
herdr machine add nat@white.follow-rankine.ts.net --label white-laris-co --remote-session laris-co
herdr --machine white-laris-co agent list
```

- Label rule (Nat: "white first"): machine first, session second. The `herdr-machine-labels` script names them `<host> · <session>`.
- To see another session of the same box, add another machine (`--machine X --session Y` is refused).
- Machines saved on m5 today (8 Nov, `herdr machine list`, herdr 0.9.5):

```text
83ef54c5  white-laris-co   nat@white.follow-rankine.ts.net          laris-co   enabled
58f05059  white-nsm        nat@white.follow-rankine.ts.net          nsm        enabled
932c2bd2  gb300            gb300                                    default    enabled
b17ec972  white-arkkra     nat@white.follow-rankine.ts.net          arkkra     enabled
c7cd7887  white-arraxccdc  nat@white.follow-rankine.ts.net          arraxccdc  enabled
be7b3860  arra-arraxccdc   <user>@<another-tailnet>.ts.net arraxccdc enabled
```

- On 3 Nov the sidebar held 12 machines; today there are 6. The list changes: read it from `herdr machine list` each time, do not remember it.
- Other subcommands: `status` (check without prompting for auth), `rename`, `remove`, `fold`/`unfold`/`fold-others`.

chunks.title: 4. Why add a machine instead of ssh-ing in and running herdr
chunks.label: herdr on many machines: add a machine, move a team to white, talk across · 4. Why add a machine instead of ssh-ing in and running herdr

images.alt: Left: herdr on m5 with white-laris-co unfolded, showing media-team, rd-team, manager-team, ccdc-team. Right: a window that ssh-ed into white and ran herdr there, showing the same tree as Local

chunks.text:
## 4. Why add a machine instead of ssh-ing in and running herdr

![Left: herdr on m5 with white-laris-co unfolded, showing media-team, rd-team, manager-team, ccdc-team. Right: a window that ssh-ed into white and ran herdr there, showing the same tree as Local](images/02-machine-vs-ssh.png)

- Frame from part 2 at 28:26. Left is m5 with the machine `white-laris-co` unfolded; right is ssh into white with herdr run inside it.
- Both sides show the same thing. Nat: you get the same thing either way.
- The difference is files. With herdr under ssh, Nat says he cannot upload a file into it; with the box added as a machine, working from m5, the file goes across.
- In practice: take a screenshot on the Mac and paste it straight into an agent that lives on white, without passing it through Discord (part 1, 08:00-08:45).

chunks.title: 5. Talk across, both ways
chunks.label: herdr on many machines: add a machine, move a team to white, talk across · 5. Talk across, both ways
chunks.text:
## 5. Talk across, both ways

```bash
herdr --machine white-laris-co agent list
herdr --machine white-laris-co agent prompt <pane> "<message>"
herdr --machine white-laris-co pane read <pane> --source recent-unwrapped --lines 40
```

- The way back: on white, save m5 as the machine `m5-laris-co`; an agent on white answers with `herdr --machine m5-laris-co agent prompt <pane> "..."`.
- Before the way back works, the user on white must reach m5 over ssh (`ssh -o BatchMode=yes ...`). On `Permission denied (publickey)`, stop and ask a human.
- `/herdr-link-talk` has a script that does all of it: `herdr-link talk nat@white.follow-rankine.ts.net neo` (dry first, then `--go`).
- Fleet rule (Nat, 5 Nov: "ask herdr say in each machine not ssh to do"): to change anything on another box, ask the agent that lives there. ssh is for read-only looks (status, logs).
- Address agents by pane id, not by name: names prefix-match, and pane ids change on every move or reboot.

chunks.title: 6. Move a whole team to white
chunks.label: herdr on many machines: add a machine, move a team to white, talk across · 6. Move a whole team to white
chunks.text:
## 6. Move a whole team to white

The real demo, part 1 at 19:45-21:00 (21:27 Bangkok time). Nat's reason: if m5 hangs, that is a risk; on white the team also saves the Mac's RAM.

1. 14:27Z Nat to LarisCo (the agent that runs the teams): "send ccdc-team to white machine"
2. LarisCo runs `just team-move ccdc white --go --merge` in a pane beside it.
3. The script opens PR #128 (`machine: white` in each member's config) and merges it.
4. One member at a time: end it on m5, wait until its process is really gone, copy the conversation, start it on white with the same conversation and the same bot.
5. The pane reports back by itself:

```text
PANE wDW:p1Y team-move ccdc white rc=0
team ccdc (laris-co/ccdc-team) -> white · session laris-co · desk ccdc-oracle stays
  plan floodboy-oracle: m5 -> white · wF7:p1 wF7 ad9a92c6 done
  plan dustboy-oracle: m5 -> white · wF8:p1 wF8 f7c606e0 done
  plan fireman-oracle: m5 -> white · wF9:p1 wF9 de5c0c13 done
PR https://github.com/laris-co/laris-team/pull/128
merged
...
just team-move ccdc white --go --merge  ... 50.940 total
```

- Result: three members on white (`w2B`, `w2C`, `w2D`, nested under the team's space), every bot on. The desk, `ccdc-oracle`, stays on m5.
- The image in §4 (left, at the bottom) shows `ccdc-team` on white holding `wt/floodboy-oracle` and `wt/dustboy-oracle` after the move.
- Back again is one command too: `just team-move ccdc m5 --go --merge`.
- The skill that does the same from a charter: `/team-ship <team> dry|go` (Nat, 2 Nov: "make go support white? make skill! for me"). Always start with `dry`.
- Start or stop a whole team on any machine: `/herdr-team-ctl start|stop|status <team> --machine <label>`.
- A team that moved can be put to sleep: see the [herdr sleep/wake](../2026-11-08_herdr-sleep-wake/) lesson.

chunks.title: 7. See every machine at once
chunks.label: herdr on many machines: add a machine, move a team to white, talk across · 7. See every machine at once
chunks.text:
## 7. See every machine at once

- `/herdr-link-check`, read-only: running sessions, reachable machines, the agents on each (`herdr-link check`).
- `/herdr-twin`: where this session runs, e.g. `nsm · 2 places · ● m5 ◐ 3 · ● white ✓ 6`.
- A crowded sidebar: m5 has `fold_machines_by_session = true`, so each session's window unfolds only the machines on the same session name and folds the rest. Or by hand: `herdr machine fold-others --same-session`.
- Folding does not disconnect. `disable` hides that machine in every m5 window.

chunks.title: 8. The skills in this family
chunks.label: herdr on many machines: add a machine, move a team to white, talk across · 8. The skills in this family
chunks.text:
## 8. The skills in this family

- `/herdr-link`: the index of the family; tells you which one to use.
- `/herdr-link-local`: move an oracle into its own session on the same machine.
- `/herdr-link-remote`: set up a worker oracle on another machine that survives a reboot (worktree, `.envrc`, systemd user unit).
- `/herdr-link-talk`: add the machine both ways and test a round trip.
- `/herdr-link-check`: see everything, change nothing.
- `/herdr-link-teardown`: remove a worker and leave the box as it was.
- `/herdr-machine-labels`, `/herdr-twin`: name and tidy the sidebar.
- `/team-ship`, `/herdr-team-ctl`: move a team, start/stop a team.
- The family's five rules: one soul = one body (a second machine gets a new name, e.g. `neo-white`), Discord on one body only, one worker per worktree, talk through herdr, back up before editing.
- To send one line to many machines with a key, see the [⌘J ⌘L](../2026-11-05_herdr-cmd-j-lesson/) lesson; to gather agents into one room, see [herdr room](../2026-10-31_herdr-room-lesson/); for every skill at once, see the [skill map](../2026-11-08_herdr-skill-map/).

chunks.title: 9. Real traps
chunks.label: herdr on many machines: add a machine, move a team to white, talk across · 9. Real traps
chunks.text:
## 9. Real traps

- **The first move broke halfway** (3 Nov, before the demo): every "end agent" step hit a Python syntax error because quoting nested across ssh; nothing moved. Fixed by going through a file, `tools/agent-quit.py`, and by finding each member on the machine it really runs on, not from its config.
- **Pane ids change**: the ccdc members were `wF1`-`wF3`, at move time `wF7`-`wF9`. The script looks them up fresh each time.
- **A bot comes up without Discord**: the config still says `machine: m5`. Merge the `machine: white` PR first (`dry` warns).
- **`--machine` cannot be combined with `--session`**: add another machine for the other session.
- **`unknown machine 'efe95d03'`**: use the full id or the label.
- **m5 has one machine list for every session**: `disable` a machine and it vanishes from every window. Use `fold`.
- **`herdr --remote` only attaches the screen**: it cannot `agent list` or `agent prompt`. Save a machine instead.
- **An agent cannot click the sidebar arrow**: tell the human, or use `prefix+w`.
- **Non-interactive ssh has no `~/.local/bin`**: put `PATH=$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH` first.
- **Machine names**: in the recording Nat typed `ssh white.local`, and the team-ship script still says `white.local`. The fleet rule now is tailscale only: use `white.follow-rankine.ts.net`.

- SKILL.md of `herdr-link`, `herdr-link-local`, `herdr-link-remote`, `herdr-link-talk`, `herdr-link-teardown`, `herdr-link-check`, `herdr-machine-labels`, `herdr-twin`, `team-ship`, `herdr-team-ctl` (the herdr-link family was built on 11 Oct 2026).
- `herdr machine list` and `herdr machine --help` on m5, 8 Nov 2026 (herdr 0.9.5).

chunks.label: herdr หลายเครื่อง: เพิ่มเครื่อง ย้ายทีมไป white คุยข้ามเครื่อง · 1. ภาพรวม

images.alt: แผนภาพ m5 กับ white ต่อกันผ่าน tailscale: m5 save white เป็น machine, white ส่งข้อความกลับด้วย herdr --machine m5-laris-co

chunks.text:
## 1. ภาพรวม

![แผนภาพ m5 กับ white ต่อกันผ่าน tailscale: m5 save white เป็น machine, white ส่งข้อความกลับด้วย herdr --machine m5-laris-co](images/00-m5-white-tailscale.png)

- **m5** คือ Mac ที่ Nat นั่งทำงาน **white** คือเครื่อง Linux (Ubuntu x86_64) ที่รับงานหนักแทน
- ทั้งคู่อยู่ใน tailnet เดียวกัน เรียกกันด้วยชื่อ MagicDNS เช่น `white.follow-rankine.ts.net`
- herdr บน m5 save white ไว้เป็น **machine** หนึ่งตัว (หนึ่ง machine = หนึ่ง session บนเครื่องนั้น)
- ssh ยังทำงานอยู่ข้างใต้ แต่ไม่มีใครต้องพิมพ์ ("ssh runs underneath; nobody types it" จาก `/herdr-link-talk`)

## 2. Local ข้างบน machine ข้างล่าง

![sidebar ของ herdr บน m5 วันที่ 3 พ.ย.: Local ข้างบนมี laris-team, aiexpo-oracle, ccdc-team ข้างล่างเป็น machine 12 ตัว เช่น black-phd, white-laris-co, gb300 จุดเขียวคือต่อได้](images/01-sidebar-local-and-machines.png)

- ภาพนี้จากคลิป part 2 นาที 27:15 Nat อธิบายว่า "ข้างบนคือ Local ก็คือเครื่องเราเอง ข้างล่างเรียกว่า Machine หรือ Remote"
- แต่ละ machine กด `▸` กางดู space ของเครื่องนั้นได้ ไม่สลับออกจากหน้าที่อยู่
- จุดเขียวข้างชื่อ = ต่ออยู่
- ใช้คีย์บอร์ด: `prefix+w` แล้ว ↑/↓ เลือก Enter ไป (จาก `/herdr-machine-labels`)
- ในคลิป part 1 นาที 07:00-07:45 Nat พิมพ์ `uname -a` ในแต่ละเครื่องให้ดูว่าอันนี้ Mac อันนี้ Linux แล้วยุบ/กางแต่ละเครื่อง ("อันนี้คือกระบวนท่าที่หนึ่ง") ส่วนนี้มีแต่เสียง จอที่อัดไว้เป็นแท็บ draw.io ว่าง ๆ เลยไม่มีภาพ

chunks.title: 3. เพิ่มเครื่อง
chunks.label: herdr หลายเครื่อง: เพิ่มเครื่อง ย้ายทีมไป white คุยข้ามเครื่อง · 3. เพิ่มเครื่อง
chunks.text:
## 3. เพิ่มเครื่อง

คำสั่งจริงจาก `/herdr-link-talk`:

```bash
# บน m5: save session laris-co ของ white เป็น machine
herdr machine add nat@white.follow-rankine.ts.net --label white-laris-co --remote-session laris-co
herdr --machine white-laris-co agent list
```

- ชื่อ label ตามกฎ Nat ("white first"): เครื่องก่อน session ทีหลัง สคริปต์ `herdr-machine-labels` ตั้งให้เป็น `<host> · <session>`
- อยากเห็นอีก session ของเครื่องเดียวกัน ต้อง add อีก machine (`--machine X --session Y` ถูกปฏิเสธ)
- เครื่องที่ save ไว้บน m5 วันนี้ (8 พ.ย., `herdr machine list`, herdr 0.9.5):

```text
83ef54c5  white-laris-co   nat@white.follow-rankine.ts.net          laris-co   enabled
58f05059  white-nsm        nat@white.follow-rankine.ts.net          nsm        enabled
932c2bd2  gb300            gb300                                    default    enabled
b17ec972  white-arkkra     nat@white.follow-rankine.ts.net          arkkra     enabled
c7cd7887  white-arraxccdc  nat@white.follow-rankine.ts.net          arraxccdc  enabled
be7b3860  arra-arraxccdc   <user>@<another-tailnet>.ts.net arraxccdc enabled
```

- วันที่ 3 พ.ย. sidebar มี 12 เครื่อง วันนี้เหลือ 6 รายการนี้เปลี่ยนได้ อ่านจาก `herdr machine list` ทุกครั้ง อย่าจำเอา
- คำสั่งย่อยอื่น: `status` (เช็กโดยไม่ถามรหัส), `rename`, `remove`, `fold`/`unfold`/`fold-others`

chunks.label: herdr หลายเครื่อง: เพิ่มเครื่อง ย้ายทีมไป white คุยข้ามเครื่อง · 4. ทำไม add machine ดีกว่า ssh เข้าไปเปิด herdr

images.alt: ซ้าย: herdr บน m5 กาง white-laris-co เห็น media-team, rd-team, manager-team, ccdc-team ขวา: หน้าต่างที่ ssh เข้า white แล้วเปิด herdr เห็นต้นไม้เดียวกันในชื่อ Local

chunks.text:
## 4. ทำไม add machine ดีกว่า ssh เข้าไปเปิด herdr

![ซ้าย: herdr บน m5 กาง white-laris-co เห็น media-team, rd-team, manager-team, ccdc-team ขวา: หน้าต่างที่ ssh เข้า white แล้วเปิด herdr เห็นต้นไม้เดียวกันในชื่อ Local](images/02-machine-vs-ssh.png)

- ภาพจาก part 2 นาที 28:26 ซ้ายคือ m5 กาง machine `white-laris-co` ขวาคือ ssh เข้า white แล้วรัน herdr ในนั้น
- สองฝั่งเห็นของเดียวกัน Nat: "มันจะได้ของแบบเดียวกันขึ้นมา"
- ต่างกันตรงไฟล์ ถ้ารัน herdr ใต้ ssh "ผมจะไม่สามารถอัปโหลดไฟล์เข้าไปได้" แต่ถ้า add เป็น machine แล้วทำงานจาก m5 "เราจะส่งไฟล์ข้ามไปได้"
- ใช้จริง: แคปหน้าจอบน Mac แล้ววางลงใน agent ที่อยู่บน white ได้เลย ไม่ต้องส่งผ่าน Discord (part 1 นาที 08:00-08:45)

chunks.title: 5. คุยข้ามเครื่อง ทั้งไปและกลับ
chunks.label: herdr หลายเครื่อง: เพิ่มเครื่อง ย้ายทีมไป white คุยข้ามเครื่อง · 5. คุยข้ามเครื่อง ทั้งไปและกลับ
chunks.text:
## 5. คุยข้ามเครื่อง ทั้งไปและกลับ

```bash
herdr --machine white-laris-co agent list
herdr --machine white-laris-co agent prompt <pane> "<ข้อความ>"
herdr --machine white-laris-co pane read <pane> --source recent-unwrapped --lines 40
```

- ขากลับ: บน white save m5 เป็น machine `m5-laris-co` แล้ว agent บน white ตอบด้วย `herdr --machine m5-laris-co agent prompt <pane> "..."`
- ก่อนขากลับใช้ได้ ต้องเช็กว่า user บน white ssh ถึง m5 ได้ (`ssh -o BatchMode=yes ...`) ถ้าเจอ `Permission denied (publickey)` ให้หยุดแล้วถามคน
- `/herdr-link-talk` มีสคริปต์ทำครบ: `herdr-link talk nat@white.follow-rankine.ts.net neo` (dry ก่อน แล้ว `--go`)
- กฎ fleet (Nat, 5 พ.ย.: "ask herdr say in each machine not ssh to do"): จะเปลี่ยนอะไรบนเครื่องอื่น ให้สั่ง agent ที่อยู่บนเครื่องนั้น ssh ใช้แค่ดูอย่างเดียว (status, log)
- เรียก agent ด้วย pane id ไม่ใช่ชื่อ ชื่อ prefix-match กันได้ และ pane id เปลี่ยนทุกครั้งที่ย้ายหรือรีบูต

chunks.title: 6. ย้ายทั้งทีมไป white
chunks.label: herdr หลายเครื่อง: เพิ่มเครื่อง ย้ายทีมไป white คุยข้ามเครื่อง · 6. ย้ายทั้งทีมไป white
chunks.text:
## 6. ย้ายทั้งทีมไป white

เดโมจริง part 1 นาที 19:45-21:00 (21:27 เวลาไทย) Nat เหตุผล: ถ้า m5 ค้างคือความเสี่ยง ให้ทีมไปอยู่ white ประหยัด RAM ฝั่ง Mac

1. 14:27Z Nat พิมพ์ถึง LarisCo (ตัวคุมทีม): "send ccdc-team to white machine"
2. LarisCo รัน `just team-move ccdc white --go --merge` ใน pane ข้าง ๆ
3. สคริปต์เปิด PR #128 (`machine: white` ใน config ของสมาชิก) แล้ว merge เอง
4. ทีละคน: ปิดที่ m5 รอให้ process หายจริง ก๊อปบทสนทนาไป แล้วเปิดใหม่บน white ด้วยบทสนทนาเดิมและ bot ตัวเดิม
5. pane ส่งผลกลับมาเอง:

```text
PANE wDW:p1Y team-move ccdc white rc=0
team ccdc (laris-co/ccdc-team) -> white · session laris-co · desk ccdc-oracle stays
  plan floodboy-oracle: m5 -> white · wF7:p1 wF7 ad9a92c6 done
  plan dustboy-oracle: m5 -> white · wF8:p1 wF8 f7c606e0 done
  plan fireman-oracle: m5 -> white · wF9:p1 wF9 de5c0c13 done
PR https://github.com/laris-co/laris-team/pull/128
merged
...
just team-move ccdc white --go --merge  ... 50.940 total
```

- ผล: สมาชิก 3 ตัวอยู่บน white (`w2B`, `w2C`, `w2D` ซ้อนใต้ space ของทีม) bot on ทุกตัว ตัว desk `ccdc-oracle` อยู่ m5 ต่อ
- ภาพใน §4 (ซ้าย ล่างสุด) คือ `ccdc-team` บน white ที่มี `wt/floodboy-oracle`, `wt/dustboy-oracle` หลังย้าย
- ขากลับก็คำสั่งเดียว: `just team-move ccdc m5 --go --merge`
- skill ที่ทำเรื่องเดียวกันจาก charter: `/team-ship <team> dry|go` (Nat, 2 พ.ย.: "make go support white? make skill! for me") เริ่มด้วย `dry` เสมอ
- เปิด/ปิดทั้งทีมบนเครื่องไหนก็ได้: `/herdr-team-ctl start|stop|status <team> --machine <label>`
- ทีมที่ย้ายแล้ว พักให้หลับได้ ดูบท [herdr sleep/wake](../2026-11-08_herdr-sleep-wake/)

chunks.title: 7. ดูทุกเครื่องในทีเดียว
chunks.label: herdr หลายเครื่อง: เพิ่มเครื่อง ย้ายทีมไป white คุยข้ามเครื่อง · 7. ดูทุกเครื่องในทีเดียว
chunks.text:
## 7. ดูทุกเครื่องในทีเดียว

- `/herdr-link-check` อ่านอย่างเดียว: session ที่รันอยู่, machine ที่ต่อได้, agent ในแต่ละเครื่อง (`herdr-link check`)
- `/herdr-twin`: session นี้รันอยู่ที่ไหนบ้าง เช่น `nsm · 2 places · ● m5 ◐ 3 · ● white ✓ 6`
- sidebar รก: บน m5 เปิด `fold_machines_by_session = true` ไว้ หน้าต่างแต่ละ session กางเฉพาะเครื่องที่ session ชื่อเดียวกัน ที่เหลือยุบ หรือสั่งเอง `herdr machine fold-others --same-session`
- ยุบ (fold) ไม่ตัดการเชื่อมต่อ ส่วน `disable` ซ่อนเครื่องนั้นในทุกหน้าต่างของ m5

chunks.title: 8. skill ในชุดนี้
chunks.label: herdr หลายเครื่อง: เพิ่มเครื่อง ย้ายทีมไป white คุยข้ามเครื่อง · 8. skill ในชุดนี้
chunks.text:
## 8. skill ในชุดนี้

- `/herdr-link`: สารบัญของชุด เลือกว่าจะใช้ตัวไหน
- `/herdr-link-local`: ย้าย oracle ไป session ของตัวเองบนเครื่องเดียวกัน
- `/herdr-link-remote`: ตั้ง worker oracle บนเครื่องอื่นให้รอดรีบูต (worktree, `.envrc`, systemd user unit)
- `/herdr-link-talk`: add machine ทั้งสองทาง ทดสอบไปกลับ
- `/herdr-link-check`: ดูทุกอย่าง ไม่แก้อะไร
- `/herdr-link-teardown`: ถอด worker ออกให้เครื่องกลับเหมือนเดิม
- `/herdr-machine-labels`, `/herdr-twin`: ตั้งชื่อและจัด sidebar
- `/team-ship`, `/herdr-team-ctl`: ย้ายทีม เปิด/ปิดทีม
- กฎห้าข้อของชุด: หนึ่งวิญญาณหนึ่งร่าง (เครื่องที่สองได้ชื่อใหม่ เช่น `neo-white`), Discord อยู่ร่างเดียว, หนึ่ง worker ต่อหนึ่ง worktree, คุยผ่าน herdr, backup ก่อนแก้
- ส่งข้อความหลายเครื่องพร้อมกันด้วยปุ่ม ดูบท [⌘J ⌘L](../2026-11-05_herdr-cmd-j-lesson/) รวม agent เป็นห้องดูบท [herdr room](../2026-10-31_herdr-room-lesson/) ภาพรวมทุก skill ดู [แผนที่ skill](../2026-11-08_herdr-skill-map/)

chunks.title: 9. กับดักที่เจอจริง
chunks.label: herdr หลายเครื่อง: เพิ่มเครื่อง ย้ายทีมไป white คุยข้ามเครื่อง · 9. กับดักที่เจอจริง
chunks.text:
## 9. กับดักที่เจอจริง

- **ย้ายครั้งแรกพังกลางทาง** (3 พ.ย. ก่อนเดโม): ขั้น "end agent" ทุกตัวขึ้น Python syntax error เพราะ quote ซ้อนกันข้าม ssh ไม่มีใครย้ายจริง แก้โดยส่งผ่านไฟล์ `tools/agent-quit.py` และหาสมาชิกจากเครื่องที่มันรันอยู่จริง ไม่ใช่จาก config
- **pane id เปลี่ยน**: สมาชิก ccdc เคยเป็น `wF1`-`wF3` ตอนย้ายเป็น `wF7`-`wF9` สคริปต์ต้องหาใหม่ทุกครั้ง
- **bot ขึ้นมาโดยไม่มี Discord**: config ยังเป็น `machine: m5` ต้อง merge PR `machine: white` ก่อน (`dry` เตือน)
- **`--machine` ใช้คู่กับ `--session` ไม่ได้**: add machine ใหม่สำหรับอีก session
- **`unknown machine 'efe95d03'`**: ใช้ id เต็มหรือ label
- **รายชื่อ machine บน m5 มีชุดเดียวทุก session**: `disable` เครื่องหนึ่ง หายจากทุกหน้าต่าง ใช้ `fold` แทน
- **`herdr --remote` แค่เปิดจอ** สั่ง `agent list`/`agent prompt` ไม่ได้ ต้อง save เป็น machine
- **agent กดลูกศรใน sidebar เองไม่ได้**: บอกคน หรือใช้ `prefix+w`
- **ssh เข้าเครื่องแล้วไม่มี `~/.local/bin`**: ใส่ `PATH=$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH` ก่อน
- **ชื่อเครื่อง**: ในคลิป Nat พิมพ์ `ssh white.local` และสคริปต์ team-ship ยังเขียน `white.local` อยู่ กฎ fleet ตอนนี้ใช้ tailscale ทางเดียว ให้ใช้ `white.follow-rankine.ts.net`

chunks.label: herdr หลายเครื่อง: เพิ่มเครื่อง ย้ายทีมไป white คุยข้ามเครื่อง · 10. ที่มา
chunks.text:
## 10. ที่มา

- คลิป Herdr part 1 (3 พ.ย. 2026, 21:07): นาที 07:00-08:45 (machine, `uname -a`, ส่งไฟล์) และ 19:45-21:00 (ย้าย ccdc-team) มีแต่เสียง ภาพจอเป็น draw.io
- คลิป Herdr part 2 (21:39): นาที 27:00-28:45 ภาพ §2 และ §4 มาจากช่วงนี้ (ตัดส่วนที่มีอีเมลและที่อยู่ LAN ออก)
- relic5 session `51fdd0de` (LarisCo, laris-team) 14:01Z-14:28Z: แผน ผล rc=0 และ PR #126/#127/#128 ([captures/relic5-team-move-2026-11-03.txt](captures/relic5-team-move-2026-11-03.txt))
- SKILL.md ของ `herdr-link`, `herdr-link-local`, `herdr-link-remote`, `herdr-link-talk`, `herdr-link-teardown`, `herdr-link-check`, `herdr-machine-labels`, `herdr-twin`, `team-ship`, `herdr-team-ctl` (ชุด herdr-link สร้าง 11 ต.ค. 2026)
- `herdr machine list` และ `herdr machine --help` บน m5 วันที่ 8 พ.ย. 2026 (herdr 0.9.5)
- กฎ fleet: tailscale เป็นเครือข่ายเดียว, ทำงานบนเครื่องอื่นผ่าน agent ของเครื่องนั้น ssh แค่ดู

## 3. Install

- One skill is one folder. Copy the folder into `~/.claude/skills/` and restart Claude Code
- Call it as `/<folder name>`, for example `/herdr-wt`
- Most skills need to run inside a herdr pane (`HERDR_ENV=1`), and many name Nat's machines (m5, white), repos and oracles; adapt them before using them elsewhere
- `.bak` files are earlier versions kept in the skill folder on m5; you do not need to copy them

For example:

```bash
# one skill / สกิลเดียว
cp -RL skills/herdr-wt ~/.claude/skills/
# all of them / ทั้งหมด
cp -RL skills/herdr* ~/.claude/skills/
```

## 5. Base, and where am I

### /herdr

What it does: The base herdr skill: the CLI to inspect and control panes, tabs, workspaces and other agents; used when herdr is named.

> `herdr` in `~/.claude/skills/` is a symlink to `~/.agents/skills/herdr`; the target's files are copied here.

- [skills/herdr/SKILL.md](skills/herdr/SKILL.md) (238 lines)

````markdown
---
name: herdr
description: "Control Herdr, a terminal multiplexer for coding agents. Use only when the user explicitly mentions Herdr or asks to use Herdr to inspect or control panes, tabs, workspaces, commands, or another agent. Do not use merely because a task could benefit from a background terminal, delegation, or parallel work. Requires HERDR_ENV=1."
---

# Herdr

Herdr organizes terminals into workspaces, tabs, and panes, recognizes coding agents running inside panes, and exposes the current session through the `herdr` CLI.

Before issuing any control command, verify that this agent is running inside a Herdr-managed pane:

```bash
test "${HERDR_ENV:-}" = 1
```

If the check fails, say that you are not running inside Herdr and stop. Do not inspect or control the focused Herdr session from outside Herdr.

When the check passes, the `herdr` binary in `PATH` talks to the current session. Use it to inspect neighboring work, create terminal layout, start agents and commands, read output, and wait for state changes.

## Learn the current CLI

The installed binary is the authority for command syntax. Start with:

```bash
herdr --help
```

Then print the relevant command group by running the group without a subcommand:

```bash
herdr agent
herdr pane
herdr workspace
herdr tab
herdr worktree
herdr terminal
herdr notification
herdr integration
herdr session
herdr machine
```

Do not run bare `herdr` for discovery; it launches or attaches the TUI. Do not probe a mutating nested command by omitting arguments. Commands such as `herdr workspace create` are valid with defaults and will execute.

Most control commands return JSON. Read identifiers and state from those responses instead of predicting them.

## Understand layout, panes, and agents

Choose the primitive that matches the job:

- Workspace, tab, and pane topology organize terminal locations.
- Pane commands control raw terminals, shells, tests, servers, input, and output.
- Agent commands control the recognized coding agent currently occupying a pane.

A pane exists whether or not it contains an agent. `agent start` requires an existing available shell pane and never creates, splits, or moves layout. Use pane commands for ordinary processes. Use agent commands when Herdr must validate agent identity or interpret `idle`, `working`, `blocked`, `done`, and `unknown` lifecycle states.

Agent commands accept either a unique live agent name or the pane ID currently hosting that agent. They do not accept terminal IDs or bare agent-kind labels. Names must match `[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}` and be unique among live agents. A name follows the current pane occupant and is cleared when that agent exits, is released, or is replaced.

`idle` and `done` both mean the agent is ready for input. The CLI/API uses the server's seen state to distinguish them; explicit focus commands mark the target seen, while reads do not. Each TUI client tracks viewed completions independently, so its Done badge can differ from the CLI or another client's badge. `blocked` means Herdr recognized an approval or question UI. `unknown` means an agent is present but Herdr cannot classify it confidently; it does not prove completion.

## Use IDs and caller context

Public IDs are opaque stable handles:

- workspace: `w1`
- tab: `w1:t1`
- pane: `w1:p1`

Closed tab and pane IDs are not reused. A pane moved into another workspace receives a new workspace-qualified pane ID. After `pane move`, continue with `.result.move_result.pane.pane_id` or the live agent name. The old value is reported as `.result.move_result.previous_pane_id`; only the moved process's inherited caller context keeps resolving that old ID, so do not use it as a general agent target.

Herdr injects the caller's context into each managed pane:

```bash
printf '%s\n' "$HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID" "$HERDR_TAB_ID" "$HERDR_PANE_ID"
```

Prefer `--current` when a pane command should target the calling pane. Omitting a target may use the UI-focused pane, which can belong to the user or another client.

Discover live state with:

```bash
herdr workspace list
herdr tab list --workspace "$HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID"
herdr pane current --current
herdr pane list --workspace "$HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID"
herdr agent list
```

Creation responses expose the IDs to use next. `workspace create` returns `.result.workspace`, `.result.tab`, and `.result.root_pane`. `tab create` returns `.result.tab` and `.result.root_pane`. `pane split` returns the new pane as `.result.pane`.

IDs and live agent names are scoped to one server. Two saved SSH machines can both have `w1:p1` or an agent named `reviewer`. Selecting a machine in the TUI does not retarget commands running in your pane: they still use the inherited session and socket context. Run remote control commands on the intended host with its explicit session, and rediscover IDs there.

`herdr machine list` lists saved connection profiles, not a cross-machine pane inventory; add `--json` for scripts. Only add, remove, enable, or disable profiles when the user asks. Removing a profile disconnects the client but does not stop remote sessions. Adding a machine uses the remote default session unless `--remote-session` is explicitly supplied. Setup asks before stopping an incompatible server and defaults to No; do not approve replacement without the user's consent. Experimental handoff is not part of `machine add`.

### Fold sidebar machines (Soul-Brews build only)

Only in our fork build (Soul-Brews-Studio/herdr `soul-brews`, installed on m5 2026-10-10;
herdr-orca-oracle #8, #9, #10, PRs #1–#4). Upstream herdr has no fold command; check with
`herdr machine --help | rg fold`. Folding is **client** presentation state, not server state:
the command edits the client's saved file
(`~/.local/state/herdr/client-shell/local-<hash>.json`, field `collapsed_machines`), and every
open client of that session applies it within about 1 s.

```bash
herdr machine folds [--json]                  # [{"id":"local","label":"Local","folded":false}, ...]
herdr machine fold <machine>... | --all       # machine = local, a label (black), or a profile id
herdr machine unfold <machine>... | --all
herdr machine toggle <machine>...
herdr machine fold-others <machine>           # fold all except it; again: unfold all
herdr machine fold-others --same-session      # open Local + machines saved for this session, fold the rest
```

**Fold by session on attach** — `[ui] fold_machines_by_session = true` in `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`
(default false; ON on m5 since 2026-10-10 10:04). When a window attaches, and when the saved machine
list changes, it opens Local plus every saved machine whose `session` equals the window's session and
folds the rest: an `nsm` window shows Local + `nsm · white` open, `black` + `white-laris-co` folded; a
`default` window folds every remote machine (none is saved under `default`). Manual folds (keys or CLI)
last until the next attach, then the rule applies again. Same matching on demand without the config:
`fold-others --same-session`. Check per session:
`herdr --session nsm machine folds`. A server still running older code reports the key as
"unknown config key" in its banner; harmless, gone after that server restarts.

- It acts on the clients of the session your pane belongs to (the inherited socket). For another
  session's windows, run it with `--session <name>`.
- Only fold what the user asked for: it changes the human's view.
- Keys (when bound in `[keys]`): `toggle_machine_collapse` (prefix+m) and
  `collapse_other_machines` (prefix+shift+m, toggle). `prefix+b` hides the whole sidebar.
- Do not fake clicks with SGR mouse escapes through WezTerm. The release half leaked as text into
  the focused pane (2026-10-10).

## Start and coordinate an agent

Default to a sibling pane in the current tab and the current working directory. Do not create a workspace, tab, worktree, or different cwd unless the user explicitly requests that topology or location.

Honor a direction requested by the user. Otherwise inspect the caller pane:

```bash
herdr pane layout --pane "$HERDR_PANE_ID"
```

Split a wide pane to the right and a narrow or tall pane down. Avoid repeated same-direction splits that create unusably narrow columns or short rows. Keep the user's focus in the calling pane and explicitly preserve the caller's working directory:

```bash
herdr pane split --current --direction right --cwd "$PWD" --no-focus
```

Replace `right` with `down` when appropriate. Read the new pane ID from `.result.pane.pane_id`.

An available shell pane must be at its interactive prompt, with the shell itself in the foreground and no foreground command, editor, or agent running. Start a supported agent in that pane with a useful unique name:

```bash
herdr agent start reviewer --kind codex --pane <returned-pane-id>
```

Use the kind requested by the user. Run `herdr agent` to inspect the installed kind list and options. Pass native agent arguments only after `--`:

```bash
herdr agent start reviewer --kind codex --pane <returned-pane-id> -- <agent-args...>
```

A successful `agent start` returns only after Herdr detects the expected agent in the same pane and considers it ready for interactive input. If the agent is blocked during startup, the command returns `agent_not_ready` immediately but keeps the name available for `agent read` and `agent send-keys`. Wait until the agent becomes idle before prompting it. Startup defaults to a 30-second timeout.

Submit work through the agent surface:

```bash
herdr agent prompt reviewer "Review the current diff and report only actionable findings." --wait --timeout 120000
```

`agent prompt` honors the pane's live bracketed-paste mode and sends text followed by encoded Enter as one ordered submission. It reports successful submission only after both have been written; that alone does not prove the agent started a turn. The submit delay grows with prompt size for Codex on Windows. It rejects an agent already waiting at an approval or question dialog with `agent_blocked` before sending any input. Inspect the blocked UI and ask the user before answering it. For normal agent work, `--wait` is enough: it waits for the first settled `idle`, `done`, or `blocked` state. Do not repeat those defaults with `--until`.

With `--wait`, a prompt sent from a non-working state must produce observed `working` or `blocked` activity. After submission, Herdr waits up to five seconds for that activity; unrelated `idle`, `done`, or session changes do not satisfy this gate. It returns `agent_prompt_stalled` if no activity is observed, or `timeout` if the caller's timeout expires first. The caller timeout includes submission time. Without a timeout, the settled-state wait is indefinite after activity is observed. This wait tracks lifecycle state, not an individual turn; if the agent is already working, completion of the active turn may satisfy it.

Use `--until` only for a state-specific workflow, such as waiting for an already-running agent to request input:

```bash
herdr agent wait reviewer --until blocked --timeout 120000
```

Without `--until`, standalone `agent wait` uses the same settled-state defaults as `agent prompt --wait`.

Use logical keys for interactive agent UI controls:

```bash
herdr agent send-keys reviewer esc
herdr agent send-keys reviewer ctrl+c
```

Herdr validates all keys before writing any bytes. Read the result through the resolved agent:

```bash
herdr agent get reviewer
herdr agent read reviewer --source recent-unwrapped --lines 120
```

If a wait fails or returns `blocked`, inspect `agent get` and `agent read` before deciding what input to send. A timeout or stalled response does not prove the prompt was never delivered; do not blindly submit it again. Use the pane surface only when raw terminal control is intentional.

## Run an ordinary command in another pane

Create a sibling pane with the same geometry rule, preserve the caller's working directory, and keep user focus unchanged:

```bash
herdr pane split --current --direction right --cwd "$PWD" --no-focus
```

Read the new pane ID from `.result.pane.pane_id`, then run and inspect the command:

```bash
herdr pane run <returned-pane-id> "just test"
herdr pane wait-output <returned-pane-id> --match "test result" --timeout 120000
herdr pane read <returned-pane-id> --source recent-unwrapped --lines 120
```

`pane run` atomically sends command text and Enter. `pane wait-output` searches the selected snapshot immediately, so output that already exists can match. Use `--match <text>` for a literal substring or `--regex <pattern>` for a Rust regular expression. Omitting `--timeout` allows an indefinite wait.

Use the read source that matches the task:

- `visible`: the currently rendered viewport.
- `recent`: recent rendered output, including soft wraps.
- `recent-unwrapped`: recent output with soft wraps joined; prefer it for logs and transcripts.
- `detection`: the plain-text bottom-buffer snapshot used for agent detection.

Use `--format ansi` when colors and terminal styling are evidence. Otherwise use text.

`--lines` asks Herdr for more rows from the pane's available screen and host scrollback. If increasing it does not reveal more of a completed response, the pane is probably running the agent on the terminal's alternate screen. Rows that leave the alternate screen do not enter Herdr's host scrollback, so a larger line count cannot recover them.

After that failed read, ask the agent to write its complete response as Markdown in a temporary directory and reply only with the file path, then read the file directly. Use this only as a fallback; do not request file output in the initial prompt.

## Safety and coordination rules

- Use `--no-focus` for background work unless the user asked to switch context.
- Use `--current`, an explicit pane ID, or a unique agent name. Do not rely on another client's focused pane.
- Parse IDs from JSON responses. Do not derive them from sidebar order or examples.
- Do not close workspaces, tabs, panes, or sessions you did not create unless the user explicitly asked. `workspace close --group` closes the primary workspace and its linked worktree workspaces; never add it merely to bypass `workspace_group_close_required`.
- Use `--trust-repository` only after the user has verified the repository. It grants per-request Git trust; it is not a routine retry for a failed worktree command.
- Client and server versions can differ after an update. Check `herdr status` before relying on new server features. A missing method is not permission to stop or upgrade a server.
- Never run `herdr server stop` from an active session unless the user explicitly intends to stop the server and its pane processes.
- Never kill the main Herdr process. Use named test sessions for experiments that need an isolated server.
- CLI server errors are JSON on stderr with exit status 1. CLI syntax errors exit with status 2.
````

### /herdr-whoami

What it does: Where THIS agent runs: machine, session/space/tab/pane, Claude session id, branch, worktree or main.

- [skills/herdr-whoami/SKILL.md](skills/herdr-whoami/SKILL.md) (35 lines)
- Other files in this folder:
  - [whoami.py](skills/herdr-whoami/whoami.py) (136 lines)

````markdown
---
name: herdr-whoami
description: Show where THIS agent is running — machine (local or over ssh), herdr session / space / tab / pane, Claude session id + transcript path, pwd vs the session's start cwd, git branch, worktree-or-main and remote. Use when the user asks "which server", "which session are we", "what herdr session", "where am I", "whoami", "session id", "pwd", "local or remote". Do NOT use to list every session on the machine (use /herdr-ls-all) or every body of one oracle (use /herdr-info).
---

# /herdr-whoami — where am I

Run it. Print the output inside one fenced block. Stop.

```bash
python3 -I ~/.claude/skills/herdr-whoami/whoami.py
```

Lines starting with `!` are warnings — mention each in one line after the block:

- `herdr pane records session X, but this process is Y` — the pane's saved agent record is stale;
  a reopen would resume the wrong conversation.
- `$HERDR_PANE_ID=X is stale (pane was moved); live pane is Y` — env is fixed at process start;
  after `herdr pane move` only herdr knows the real pane. The rows show the live one.
- `pwd moved away from the session's start cwd` — the Bash tool `cd`'d somewhere; git rows describe
  the new pwd, not the repo the session started in.

## Sources

| row | from |
|---|---|
| host / user / reached | `hostname`, `$USER`, `$SSH_CONNECTION` (set = remote ssh login) |
| herdr session / space / tab / pane | `$HERDR_SESSION`, `$HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID` + `herdr workspace list` label, `$HERDR_TAB_ID`, `$HERDR_PANE_ID` |
| pane cwd | `herdr pane get` → `foreground_cwd` |
| session id / name / version / start cwd | `$CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, `~/.claude/sessions/$CLAUDE_PID.json` |
| transcript | `~/.claude/projects/<start cwd, non-alnum → ->/<id>.jsonl` |
| git | `git status -sb`, `--git-common-dir` (worktree vs main), `remote get-url origin` |

Env vars are read, never the socket of another session: `herdr` with no `--session` hits
`$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`, which is this pane's own session — exactly what is wanted here.
````

### /herdr-info

What it does: Every body of one oracle on this machine, in and out of herdr, plus Discord, checked against the one-soul-many-bodies rules.

- [skills/herdr-info/SKILL.md](skills/herdr-info/SKILL.md) (79 lines)
- Other files in this folder:
  - [SKILL.md.bak-20261005-wt](skills/herdr-info/SKILL.md.bak-20261005-wt) (74 lines)
  - [herdr-info.py](skills/herdr-info/herdr-info.py) (333 lines)
  - [herdr-info.py.bak-2026-10-05](skills/herdr-info/herdr-info.py.bak-2026-10-05) (292 lines)
  - [herdr-info.py.bak-20261005-wt](skills/herdr-info/herdr-info.py.bak-20261005-wt) (302 lines)

````markdown
---
name: herdr-info
description: Show every body of ONE oracle on this machine — every herdr session, space and pane where it runs (main checkout or worktree), anything running outside herdr, its Discord connections — check the one-soul-many-bodies rules (one conversation id per body, one Discord connection per bot), and draw each tab that holds it as a layout card. Use when the user says "herdr-info <oracle>", "where is <oracle> running", "list all <oracle>", "list all working pulse", "draw <oracle> layout", or "how many <oracle> bodies". Also takes a herdr SPACE name ("herdr-info office") when no oracle has that name: lists every pane in that space. Do NOT use for one repo's worktree and git status (use /herdr-tree), or to move an oracle (use /herdr-bring).
argument-hint: "<oracle|space> [--no-layout] [--json] [--width N]"
---

# /herdr-info — one soul, every body

An oracle can run in several herdr sessions, spaces and panes at once, in its main checkout or in
worktrees. This finds all of them on this machine and draws where they sit.

## Run

```bash
python3 ~/.claude/skills/herdr-info/herdr-info.py <oracle>              # e.g. pulse
python3 ~/.claude/skills/herdr-info/herdr-info.py <space>               # e.g. office (when no oracle has that name)
python3 ~/.claude/skills/herdr-info/herdr-info.py <oracle> --no-layout  # table only
python3 ~/.claude/skills/herdr-info/herdr-info.py <oracle> --json       # raw
python3 ~/.claude/skills/herdr-info/herdr-info.py <oracle> --width 96   # fit N columns: shortens Where, wraps long lines
```

How to show it (Nat, 2026-10-05):
1. Everything the script prints goes **inside one fenced block**: header, layout cards, agents table,
   shell panes, warnings. All of it is box drawing, which only lines up in monospace.
2. The agents table (`Session | Pane | Agent | State | Where | Up`) has one row per window, i.e. per
   herdr session (a terminal window shows one session; its spaces are pages in the sidebar). Each cell
   holds one line per agent, so a row reads across: line 2 of every column is the same agent. The
   script draws it itself: markdown table cells cannot hold line breaks. `Up` is the agent process's
   age; the agent that ran the command shows `this conversation`, and its line comes first.
3. After the block: one line per warning and per body worth acting on (an idle agent whose worktree
   is merged, a body outside herdr).

## Name lookup: oracle first, then space

`<name>` is tried as an oracle first: any ghq checkout named `<name>` or `<name>-oracle`. If none
exists, it is tried as a herdr space label (case-insensitive) in every running session, and every
pane in that space is listed, whatever repo it runs in. The header then reads `space <name> - ...`.
Neither found: exit 1. (Nat, 2026-10-05: "first track oracle name if not found go these space name")

## What it reads

| source | for |
|---|---|
| `ghq list -p` | the oracle's repos: every checkout named `<oracle>` or `<oracle>-oracle`, any org |
| `git -C <repo> worktree list --porcelain` | linked worktrees that live OUTSIDE the repo folder (`~/.herdr/worktrees/…`, orca, incubate); panes there count too, shown as `wt ~/.herdr/worktrees/<repo>/<name>` |
| `herdr session list --json`, then `herdr --session <s> api snapshot` per running session | panes whose folder is in those repos or their worktrees: agent, status, conversation id, space, tab layout |
| `herdr --session <s> pane process-info --pane <p>` | which processes each agent pane owns |
| `ps` + `lsof` cwd | claude / codex processes in those repos that no herdr pane owns (tmux, plain terminals). A desktop app's own helpers are skipped: an executable inside an `.app` bundle, or `codex sandbox` / `codex app-server` (ChatGPT.app runs these with whatever folder it last used) |

Fixed 2026-10-05 (Nat: "fix herdr-info"): before, an agent in `~/.herdr/worktrees/neo-oracle/…` was
missing from the table, and ChatGPT.app's codex helpers showed up as "6 outside herdr" for neo.
Checked on the-oracle-voice: shell `wAT:p1` in `~/.herdr/worktrees/the-oracle-voice/worktree-brave-forest-2d98` is now listed.
| `bun … discord` plugin processes + their parent's cwd | Discord connections, by `DISCORD_STATE_DIR` |

Always passes `--session <name>` explicitly: inside a herdr pane, `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` would otherwise
silently point every call at the caller's own session.

## Warnings

| warning | why it matters |
|---|---|
| one conversation id live in 2+ bodies | both write one transcript; it branches and a later resume can come back as the other body |
| 2+ Discord connections on one state dir | every message reaches every connection (seen 2026-10-03 on atlas, twice) |
| Discord plugin with no `DISCORD_STATE_DIR` | the official plugin then falls back to `~/.claude/channels/discord` (mawjs's folder); a repo's own plugin (e.g. `bun .discord/mcp.ts`) may read its own `.discord` — check `ps -o command=` |

## Layout card

Printed FIRST, right after the two header lines; the table, shells, Discord and warnings follow
(Nat, 2026-10-05: "layout first list later"). Each tab that holds at least one body is drawn from
herdr's own pane rectangles, two cards per row.
Proportions are kept but compressed so every pane gets room for its label: pane id, agent and
status, and the first 8 characters of the conversation id. Other panes in the same tab (shells,
other agents) are drawn too, so the card shows what the body sits next to.

## Related

- `/herdr-tree` — one repo: checkouts, git state, phase, and the layout of its open spaces
- `/herdr-bring` — move a body into this herdr server (kill before resume)
- `herdr-layout --pane <id>` (`~/.local/bin`) — one tab in full detail
````

### /herdr-tree

What it does: This repo's main checkout and every worktree as a tree, with herdr space, agent status and git status.

- [skills/herdr-tree/SKILL.md](skills/herdr-tree/SKILL.md) (50 lines)
- Other files in this folder:
  - [herdr-tree.py](skills/herdr-tree/herdr-tree.py) (279 lines)
  - [herdr-tree.py.bak-2026-10-05](skills/herdr-tree/herdr-tree.py.bak-2026-10-05) (188 lines)

````markdown
---
name: herdr-tree
description: List this repo's main checkout and every git worktree as a tree, with the herdr space, agent status (working/idle/blocked/closed) and git status (ahead/behind, changed, untracked, locked) per row. Use when the user says "herdr-tree", "list our worktrees", "tree status", "what worktrees do we have here", or wants the herdr sidebar view in the conversation. Do NOT use to create a worktree (use /herdr-wt) or to move an oracle into herdr (use /herdr-bring).
---

# /herdr-tree

The herdr sidebar tree, in the conversation. Reads `git worktree list` (so worktrees closed in herdr still appear), joins it with `herdr workspace list` and `herdr pane list`, and asks git about every checkout in parallel. About 0.15 s.

## Run

```bash
python3 ~/.claude/skills/herdr-tree/herdr-tree.py            # repo of the current directory
python3 ~/.claude/skills/herdr-tree/herdr-tree.py <path>     # any repo
python3 ~/.claude/skills/herdr-tree/herdr-tree.py --json     # raw rows
python3 ~/.claude/skills/herdr-tree/herdr-tree.py --no-layout  # tree only
python3 ~/.claude/skills/herdr-tree/herdr-tree.py --session nsm  # another herdr session: one tree + layout per repo in it
```

With `--session`, `open`/`closed` is relative to that session: a worktree open in `default` shows as
`closed` in an `nsm` tree.

## Layout (after the tree)

Every open space of the repo, tab by tab, drawn from herdr's own pane rectangles (`herdr api snapshot`
→ `layouts[].panes[].rect`), scaled to 70 columns. Each box shows the pane id, the agent name and status
(or `shell`), and the pane's folder relative to the repo. A tab with one pane prints as one line instead
of a box. Panes too small for text still get their borders. Only the default herdr session is read, the
same as the tree; another session's layout needs `herdr --session <name> api snapshot`.

Print the output as-is in a fenced block, then add one line per thing that needs attention (a PRUNABLE row, a `no-upstream` branch with unpushed work, a row that is `closed` but dirty).

## Columns

| column | meaning |
|---|---|
| glyph + label | `*` working, `o` idle, `!` blocked, `?` unknown, `-` not open in herdr |
| status, space | herdr agent status and space id (`closed` if no space) |
| agent | agent kinds running in that space |
| branch | checked-out branch |
| flags | `upN` ahead, `dnN` behind, `~N` changed, `?N` untracked, `locked`, `PRUNABLE`, `no-upstream`, `clean` |
| last | short sha and age of the newest commit |

`<-- here` marks the checkout the command ran in.

## Traps

- `no-upstream` on a worktree branch is normal until the first push. It is not an error.
- A row with `closed` still has files on disk. Removing the herdr space does not remove the worktree.
- Needs `herdr` on PATH. Without a running herdr server the tree still prints, with every row `closed`.
````

### /herdr-structure

What it does: A whole herdr session drawn as a tree: spaces, rooms (2+ agents), agent names, status, team lead and "me".

- [skills/herdr-structure/SKILL.md](skills/herdr-structure/SKILL.md) (39 lines)

````markdown
---
name: herdr-structure
description: Draw a whole herdr session as a tree: every space, which spaces are rooms (2+ agents), each pane's agent name, status and conversation id, the team lead (from the pulse-oracle team charters) and "me". Works for m5 sessions and saved remote machines (white-nsm, white-phonebooth, ...), or all at once. Use when the user says "herdr-structure", "show the structure", "nsm see structure on white", "what is in session X", "draw the session", or wants the team layout of a session in the conversation. Do NOT use for one repo's worktrees and git status (use /herdr-tree) or for every body of one oracle (use /herdr-info).
---

# /herdr-structure

One session, one tree. Reads `herdr workspace list`, `pane list` and `agent list` for the target
(local session or `--machine`), so it is live, not a saved state file. About 1 s per target.

## Run

```bash
herdr-structure                          # m5, session laris-co (or $HERDR_SESSION)
herdr-structure --session phonebooth     # another m5 session
herdr-structure --machine white-nsm      # a saved remote machine = that machine's session
herdr-structure --all                    # every running m5 session + every enabled saved machine
herdr-structure --json                   # raw rows
```

## Reading it

```
white-nsm  ·  7 spaces, 8 agents
├─ w7   nonsense-matters-oracle        w7:p1   idle       <- lead
├─ wG   media-team  (room, 2)
│    ├─ wG:p1   dakanda-oracle             idle
│    └─ wG:p2   pigment-nsm                idle
└─ wH   xiaoer-oracle                  wH:p1   idle
```

- A space with 2+ agents is drawn as a room, with its panes under it.
- `<- lead` = the `lead:` of a charter in `laris-co/pulse-oracle/teams/*.yaml` (local main; an unmerged charter is not seen).
- `<- me` = the pane this runs from (local sessions only).
- `(shell, no agent)` = a space with no running agent (after a reboot, or a job pane).
- Conversation ids are empty for remote machines without herdr's claude integration (white).

After drawing, say in one or two lines what stands out: an agent missing from its room, a space with no
agent, a lead not running.
````

### /herdr-neighbors

What it does: Survey every pane around you (four directions and the workspace) as agent or shell before touching any. Read-only.

- [skills/herdr-neighbors/SKILL.md](skills/herdr-neighbors/SKILL.md) (108 lines)

````markdown
---
name: herdr-neighbors
description: Survey every pane around you before you touch any of them — all four directions plus the whole workspace, each reported as agent-or-shell with its name, kind, status and cwd. Read-only. Use when the user says "check neighbours", "who is around", "who else is here", "what panes are open", "is anyone next to me", or before any fan-out where you are about to message or run something in more than one pane. To read ONE buddy's scrollback use /herdr-peek; to message one use /herdr-hey.
argument-hint: ""
---

# /herdr-neighbors — know who is around before you touch anything

Read-only. Sends nothing anywhere. This is the survey you run **before** [[herdr-hey]]
or [[herdr-pane-run]], not instead of them.

The one question it answers that nothing else does: **which panes hold agents and which
hold shells**, for every pane near you at once. Get that wrong and a shell command lands
in an agent's prompt, or prose executes in a shell.

## Run it

```bash
me="${HERDR_PANE_ID:-$(herdr pane current | python3 -c "import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['result']['pane']['pane_id'])")}"
echo "me = $me"

# 1. adjacency — who is literally beside me, per direction
for d in left right up down; do
  n=$(herdr pane neighbor --pane "$me" --direction "$d" 2>/dev/null \
    | python3 -c "import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['result']['neighbor'].get('neighbor_pane_id',''))")
  printf '  %-6s %s\n' "$d" "${n:-—}"
done

# 2. occupancy — every pane in my workspace, agent or shell
herdr pane list | python3 -c "
import json,sys,subprocess
me=sys.argv[1]; ws=me.split(':')[0]
agents={}
for a in json.loads(subprocess.run(['herdr','agent','list'],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout)['result']['agents']:
    agents[a['pane_id']]=a
for p in json.load(sys.stdin)['result']['panes']:
    if p.get('workspace_id')!=ws: continue
    pid=p['pane_id']; a=agents.get(pid)
    who=f\"{a['agent']} '{a.get('name') or '(unnamed)'}' [{a['agent_status']}]\" if a else 'bare shell'
    print(f\"  {pid}{' (me)' if pid==me else ''}  {who}  {p.get('cwd','')}\")
" "$me"
```

## Read BOTH lists — they answer different questions

| list | answers |
|---|---|
| adjacency (`pane neighbor`) | which pane is *beside* me, per direction — what `/herdr-peek right` will target |
| occupancy (`pane list` + `agent list`) | who exists at all, including panes that are **not** a directional neighbour |

They disagree routinely, and that is not a bug. Measured 2026-09-19: `wJ:p1` and `wJ:p3`
were the only two panes in the workspace, so occupancy showed both — but adjacency
showed `right → wJ:p3` and **nothing** for left, up, down. A pane can exist in the tab
and be reachable by no direction at all once the layout has more than two panes.

Never substitute one for the other. "It is the only other pane, so it must be my
neighbour" holds in a two-pane tab and breaks silently in three.

## `herdr agent list` is the check that matters — not `pane list`

`pane list` gives you `cwd`, and **cwd does not say whether anyone is home**. A pane
sitting in a repo directory looks identical whether an agent occupies it or it is an
idle shell.

Measured 2026-09-19: `herdr pane run <pane> 'npx wrangler tail …'` was aimed at a pane
believed free, after checking `pane list` and reading only the cwd. It held a live
Claude agent. The command arrived as a **user turn** and that agent began acting on it.

```
pane holds an agent  ->  herdr agent prompt <name>    (a message)
pane holds a shell   ->  herdr pane run <pane> 'cmd'  (a command)
```

## Expect the layout to flicker

The same adjacency call returned `wJ:p3`, then nothing, then `wJ:p3` again inside a
minute while the pane existed the whole time — the layout was mid-change as the human
moved focus. **One empty survey means "not right now", not "nobody is there."** Re-run
before concluding you are alone.

## Traps

**`--current` is not uniform across subcommands** (herdr 0.9.1):

| call | resolves to |
|---|---|
| `herdr pane current` | your own pane — stable |
| `herdr pane neighbor --current` | the **focused** pane — moves when the human clicks |

Use `--pane "$HERDR_PANE_ID"` everywhere. Found by glyph-codex, 2026-09-19.

**`pane_id` is the source, `neighbor_pane_id` is the answer.** `pane neighbor` returns
both; the obvious key is you. A `.get('pane_id')` fallback surveys yourself.

**The key is ABSENT when there is no neighbour** — the response drops to
`direction`, `layout`, `pane_id`, so `n['neighbor_pane_id']` raises `KeyError` instead
of reporting "none". Always `.get(..., '')`.

**Names are not durable.** herdr's docs: *"A name follows the current pane occupant and
is cleared when that agent exits, is released, or is replaced."* A name that vanishes
fails loudly (`agent_not_found`); a stale pane id delivers to whoever inherited it,
silently. Re-survey after any gap rather than reusing a name you cached.

## Related

[[herdr-peek]] reads one buddy's scrollback. [[herdr-hey]] messages one. [[herdr-buddy]]
creates one. [[herdr-pane-run]] runs a command in a bare shell pane. [[herdr]] is the
CLI reference.
````

### /herdr-twin

What it does: Find every machine running the same session, with agent count and status, and toggle the sidebar's twin mode.

- [skills/herdr-twin/SKILL.md](skills/herdr-twin/SKILL.md) (66 lines)

````markdown
---
name: herdr-twin
description: Resolve the local herdr session and list every machine running the same session, grouped like "nsm · 2 places · ● m5 ◐ 3 · ● white ✓ 6" (agent count + status per machine); toggle twin mode so the herdr sidebar shows only those machines (on the Soul-Brews build prefer ui.fold_machines_by_session / herdr machine fold-others --same-session, which folds instead of disabling); group every session the same way. Use when the user says "twin", "/herdr-twin", "herdr twin", "show my twin", "which machines run this session", "group by session", "show only matching sessions", "toggle remote machines", "hide the other machines", "show all machines again". Old names /herdr-match and /herdr-machines-match (aliases kept). Do NOT use to rename labels (use /herdr-machine-labels), to add/remove machines (herdr machine add/remove), or to list Claude conversation ids per repo (use /claude-twins).
argument-hint: "[on | off | toggle | groups | list | <session>]"
---

# /herdr-twin — this session, every place it runs

Calling `/herdr-twin` with no argument = **resolve + list, no change**:

```text
$ herdr-twin
  nsm                          2 places
    ● m5           ◐  3   local
    ● white        ✓  6   white · nsm
  twin mode: herdr-twin on · back: herdr-twin off · every session: herdr-twin groups
```

| command | does |
|---|---|
| `herdr-twin` | local session = `$HERDR_SESSION` (else the name in `$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`, else `default`); every saved machine on that session, with its agents |
| `herdr-twin groups` | every session (running here + every saved machine), one block per session name |
| `herdr-twin on` | twin view: `herdr machine fold-others --same-session` — folds the other machines **in this session's windows only**, nothing disconnects (Soul-Brews build). Upstream herdr (white) falls back to `machine disable`, which hides them in every window — avoid on m5 |
| `herdr-twin off` | unfold every machine (fold build) / enable every machine (upstream fallback) |
| `herdr-twin toggle` | on ⇄ off |
| `herdr-twin list` | saved machines and state |
| `… --session nsm` / `herdr-twin nsm` | name the session instead of resolving it |

Icons: `◐` some agent working · `!` some blocked · `✓` all ready (idle/done) · `○` hidden (a disabled machine
cannot be queried: "machine … is disabled"). The number is the agent count from `herdr agent list` (local) and
`herdr --machine <id> agent list` (remote).

In nonsense-matters-oracle: `just twin` · `just twin groups|on|off|toggle|list` (script vendored at
`tools/herdr-twin`). Global: `~/.local/bin/herdr-twin`.

Nat, 2026-10-10: *"toggle remote machine name match local session name"* → *"resolve current session id and
list all remote match session id like this we can group"* (a mock: `nsm · 2 places · m5 ◐ 2 · white ✓ 6`).

## Fold instead of hide (Soul-Brews build, 2026-10-10)

On m5's herdr (fork `soul-brews`, herdr-orca-oracle #10) the sidebar does this by itself:
`[ui] fold_machines_by_session = true` in `~/.config/herdr/config.toml` (ON on m5 since 10:04).
On attach, each window opens Local + the saved machines whose session equals its own, and folds
the rest. An `nsm` window: `▾ Local`, `▸ black`, `▸ white-laris-co`, `▾ nsm · white`.

| want | prefer | why |
|---|---|---|
| sidebar shows only this session's twins | the config (already on) or `herdr machine fold-others --same-session` | per session, per window; nothing disconnects; folded machines stay queryable |
| really drop the others from every window | `herdr-twin on` (disable) | one list per computer: hides them in every session's window |
| text view with agent counts | `herdr-twin` / `groups` | unchanged |

Check a session's folds: `herdr --session nsm machine folds`. Manual folds last until the next attach.
Upstream herdr (and white, unless it gets our build) has no fold command: there, `herdr-twin on` is
still the only switch.

## Rules
- Disable (twin mode) is safe: profile kept, remote herdr server, sessions and agents keep running; only this
  computer's herdr clients disconnect. One saved-machine list per computer — twin mode in an `nsm` window hides
  `white · laris-co` in a `laris-co` window too.
- Upstream herdr has no grouped node and no auto-expand (docs "Connecting machines": a machine profile targets one
  remote session). Our build adds the auto-expand per session (above), still no grouped node: this skill
  stays the text view.
- Pairs with `/herdr-machine-labels` (`<host> · <session>`) and `/claude-twins` (conversation ids per repo).


2026-10-10 11:0x: herdr-orca-oracle (for Nat) — my `herdr-twin on` at 10:55 disabled black + white · laris-co in every m5 window. Fixed the same hour: on/off/toggle fold per window when `herdr machine --help` lists `fold-others`.
````
